title: EY Foundation Smart Futures 2026/27 | Paid Work Experience, Training and Mentoring for Young People in the UK
summary: The EY Foundation Smart Futures programme is a career development opportunity designed to help young people gain practical experience of the workplace, develop employability skills and receive professional mentoring before they leave school. The programme combines paid work experience, interactive employability skills training and business mentoring , with opportunities across different sectors and locations in the UK. The EY Foundation currently lists 2026/27 Smart Futures programmes as open for applications , with programmes available in locations including London, Birmingham, Manchester, Liverpool, Bradford, Newcastle and Aberdeen, among others. Unlike a traditional work-experience placement, Smart Futures combines workplace exposure with structured training and mentoring. Participants can explore different industries, develop transferable skills, build professional networks and receive guidance as they consider their next steps into employment or higher education. About the Smart Futures Programme Smart Futures is an EY Foundation programme for young people in Year 12 in England or S5 in Scotland . Participants receive paid work experience with employer partners, employability skills training and support from a business mentor. The programme is designed to help young people understand the world of work and develop skills that can support their transition into employment, apprenticeships or university. The EY Foundation describes its wider programme offer as supporting young people with paid employability training and work experience, alongside mentoring and, where needed, support with travel costs. What Does Smart Futures Offer? Successful participants can benefit from several components throughout the programme. 1. Paid Work Experience Participants receive real-world experience with one of the programme s employer partners. This provides an opportunity to experience a professional working environment, understand workplace expectations and gain practical knowledge that can strengthen future applications for jobs, apprenticeships or university. The work experience can also help participants understand what different careers are actually like before making important decisions about their future. 2. Employability Skills Training The programme includes up to two weeks of employability skills training and interactive workshops . Training can include activities designed to develop: Communication Teamwork Confidence Networking Workplace awareness Professional skills Career planning Understanding of different industries and organisations Participants also have opportunities to meet other young people taking part in Smart Futures. 3. Business Mentoring Participants receive support from a business mentor who can help them understand their options and prepare for the transition into professional working life or higher education. Mentoring can provide guidance around career decisions, workplace expectations and the first steps towards a future career. 4. Alumni and Networking Opportunities Participants can also be invited to alumni events through the EY Foundation s Limitless Series during their final year at school or college. The programme provides opportunities to practise networking and build connections with professionals and other young people. Smart Futures Career Areas One of the major strengths of Smart Futures is the range of career-focused programmes available. The programme is not limited to students who already know exactly what career they want. The EY Foundation states that its different programmes can provide workplace experience and transferable skills even for young people who are still exploring their options. Some of the programme areas include: Smart Futures Business and Finance Sector: Professional Services This programme is aimed at young people interested in careers such as accounting, consulting and other professional services. It is particularly relevant to students considering a high-level or degree apprenticeship after school or college. Secure Futures Sector: Security Secure Futures introduces participants to careers within the security sector, including work connected to keeping people safe online, in workplaces, homes and public spaces. Tech Futures Sector: Technology Tech Futures provides exposure to the technology and digital sector. Participants can gain insight into technological careers while receiving work experience and mentorship from professionals working on digital developments. Smart Futures Banking and Finance Sector: Banking This programme introduces participants to different careers within banking and finance. Areas covered can include: Branch banking Technology Sustainability Marketing Risk Relationship management Smart Futures Business and Technology Sectors: Professional Services, Finance and Technology This programme is designed for young people interested in exploring career opportunities across professional services, finance and technology. Impactful Futures Sector: Charity Impactful Futures provides young people with an opportunity to explore careers in the charity sector and understand the range of professional roles that contribute to positive social change. STEM Futures Sectors: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics STEM Futures provides insight into careers connected to science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Data Driven Futures Sectors: Data, Business Analysis and Risk This programme introduces young people to data-focused careers, including the work of actuaries and professionals who use mathematics, data and risk analysis to help organisations make informed decisions. Private Equity Futures Sector: Private Equity Private Equity Futures provides an introduction to the private equity sector and the role investment can play in supporting business growth and innovation. Real Estate Futures Sector: Real Estate Real Estate Futures introduces participants to the property sector and careers connected with the development and management of buildings, communities and cities. 2026/27 Smart Futures Programme Dates and Locations The current EY Foundation application page lists multiple 2026/27 programmes as open , with dates varying according to location and programme. Examples include: Programme Location Programme dates Smart Futures Business Technology North West – Manchester/Liverpool 23 Nov–2 Dec 2026 Smart Futures Business Technology Bradford 15–24 Feb 2027 Impactful Futures North West – Manchester/Liverpool 15–24 Feb 2027 Smart Futures Business Technology Birmingham 30 Nov–9 Dec 2026 Smart Futures Business Technology Aberdeen 12–21 Oct 2026 Smart Futures Business Finance Glasgow 7–16 Jun 2027 Smart Futures Business Technology London 15–24 Feb 2027 Smart Futures Banking Finance London 30 Mar–8 Apr 2027 Tech Futures London 1–4 Jun and 26 Jul 2027 Real Estate Futures London 1–4 Jun and 2–5 Aug 2027 Private Equity Futures London 26 Jul–4 Aug 2027 The EY Foundation notes that applicants must be based in the relevant delivery location for the programme they select. The full list of programmes, locations and dates is available on the official application page. Who Can Apply? The Smart Futures eligibility criteria are designed specifically for young people who may face financial or socioeconomic barriers to accessing professional work experience. Applicants must meet the following requirements. Financial Eligibility Applicants must either: Have been eligible for Free School Meals at any time during the previous two years , or Be eligible for a college bursary or Education Maintenance Allowance (EMA) . Age and Education Applicants must also: Be in Year 12 in England or Fifth Year (S5) in Scotland . Be 16 or 17 years old during the programme . Attend a state school . Be studying an eligible combination of qualifications, including A-levels, International Baccalaureate, BTEC Level 3s, National 5s or Highers. Have achieved at least Grade 4 in English Language or English Functional Skills Level 2 , subject to programme-specific exceptions. Applicants should also be ambitious and motivated to learn about the world of work and interested in gaining paid work experience that could support their future employment or university plans. Additional Requirements for Business and Finance The Smart Futures Business and Finance programme has additional academic requirements. Applicants must have: At least Grade 6 in GCSE Maths for London-based programmes. At least Grade 5 in GCSE Maths for other locations. Be on track to achieve 112 UCAS points from their top three A Levels or five Highers. Have a strong interest in applying for a high-level or degree apprenticeship after school or college. The EY Foundation also states that there is no GCSE English Language or English Functional Skills requirement for relevant North/Newcastle-based Smart Futures programmes for applicants living in Newcastle. Does Your Subject of Study Matter? For most Smart Futures programmes, applicants do not need to be studying business-related subjects. The programme is designed to give young people exposure to different industries and transferable skills, meaning students from different academic backgrounds can apply if they meet the relevant eligibility requirements. However, individual programmes such as Business and Finance can have additional qualification requirements, so applicants should always check the requirements for their chosen programme. How to Apply The current application process involves two main stages . Step 1: Complete the Online Application Applicants first need to register and complete a short online application form. The EY Foundation recommends using a personal email address rather than a school email address where possible. Applicants will select their preferred programme and location and provide information about their background and circumstances. The Foundation states that most Smart Futures programmes do not depend on previous work experience, grades or qualifications beyond the specific eligibility requirements. Step 2: Telephone Interview Applicants who successfully progress from the initial application will be invited to a short telephone interview. The interview can take up to 30 minutes . Candidates may be asked about: Their experiences Their strengths Their motivations Their future aspirations Examples from school or home life The interview is intended to help the EY Foundation understand each applicant s individual strengths and motivation for joining Smart Futures. Application Deadline There is no single overall deadline stated for all Smart Futures 2026/27 programmes on the current application page. Instead, applications are listed according to individual programme dates and locations, with several 2026/27 programmes currently marked Open . Applicants should therefore check the specific programme they want to join and apply as early as possible. How to Choose the Right Smart Futures Programme Applicants should consider their career interests when selecting a programme. For example: Interested in technology and digital careers ? Consider Tech Futures or Business Technology. Interested in banking and finance ? Consider Banking Finance. Interested in accounting or consulting ? Consider Business and Finance. Interested in STEM careers ? Consider STEM Futures. Interested in investment ? Consider Private Equity Futures. Interested in property and urban development ? Consider Real Estate Futures. Interested in charities and social impact ? Consider Impactful Futures. Interested in data, mathematics and risk ? Consider Data Driven Futures. You do not necessarily need to have your entire career mapped out before applying. The programme is also designed to help young people explore different professional environments and develop transferable skills. Evidence of Programme Impact The EY Foundation reports that 96% of young people surveyed said they were extremely or very confident that the support they received would help them get a job after education. The Foundation also reports that 99% of respondents rated Smart Futures as Good or Excellent after taking part. These figures were based on 284 respondents. How to Apply for Smart Futures Young people interested in the programme should review the available 2026/27 programme dates and locations and select a programme for which they meet the eligibility requirements. The official EY Foundation application page contains the current programme schedule and application process. Apply here: EY Foundation Smart Futures – How to Apply Conclusion The EY Foundation Smart Futures programme provides eligible young people with an opportunity to gain paid work experience, develop workplace skills, receive professional mentoring and explore different career sectors. With programmes covering areas such as technology, banking, finance, professional services, STEM, data, private equity, real estate, security and charity work , participants can choose an opportunity aligned with their interests while gaining practical exposure to the world of work. The 2026/27 programme cycle is currently open , with different dates and locations available across the UK. Because individual programmes have different schedules and locations, prospective applicants should check the official application page carefully and submit an application for a suitable programme. Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: Charlotte Community Foundation Fall 2026 Grants | Up to $15,000 for Local Nonprofits
summary: The Charlotte Community Foundation (CCF) has opened its Fall 2026 competitive grant cycle , providing funding opportunities for eligible nonprofit organisations serving Charlotte County, Florida . The Fall 2026 cycle will distribute $195,000 in donor-designated funding through two grant opportunities focused on specific areas of community need. Eligible organisations can apply for funding supporting work in health care, housing insecurity, seniors, veterans and youth . Applications opened on September 1, 2026 , and must be submitted by September 29, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. About the Charlotte Community Foundation Fall 2026 Grants The Charlotte Community Foundation is a philanthropic organisation dedicated to strengthening the quality of life in Charlotte County, Florida . For the Fall 2026 grant cycle, CCF is offering competitive funding through donor-designated funds supporting specific areas of local nonprofit service delivery. The cycle includes program grants supporting organisations working in housing insecurity and health care , while the broader designated funding areas for the cycle also include seniors, veterans and youth . Funding Available The Fall 2026 cycle includes: Housing Insecurity CCF will provide four grants of $15,000 for organisations addressing housing insecurity. Eligible organisations should provide services such as: Direct services for people experiencing housing insecurity. Homelessness prevention programmes. Housing solutions. Outreach services. Support systems aimed at reducing or ending homelessness. Programmes serving children and youth experiencing homelessness are especially encouraged to apply. Health Care CCF will also provide four grants of $15,000 for organisations working in health care. Eligible applicants may provide: Direct health-related services. Access to quality health care. Initiatives designed to improve health outcomes. Physical health services. Mental and behavioural health services. Preventive and primary care. Nutrition and wellness programmes. CCF takes a broad approach to the definition of health and health care for this funding opportunity. Total Funding The two $15,000 grant areas described above represent: $60,000 for Housing Insecurity $60,000 for Health Care $120,000 total for these two programme grant areas The Foundation s Fall 2026 cycle overall is described as distributing $195,000 in donor-designated contributions through two grant opportunities covering five local nonprofit service areas. Who Can Apply? The Fall 2026 grants are intended for nonprofit organisations that meet CCF s eligibility requirements. Organisations must: Be a nonprofit organisation with 501(c)(3) status , unless another status has been approved by CCF. Have received their tax-exempt determination letter from the IRS. Align with the mission of the Charlotte Community Foundation. Be located in or provide services in Charlotte County, Florida . Use the grant funding within Charlotte County. An organisation does not necessarily have to be headquartered in Charlotte County. However, the funded activities must take place within the county. Funding Areas for the Fall 2026 Cycle CCF identifies five designated areas for its Fall 2026 grants: Health Care Housing Insecurity Seniors Veterans Youth An organisation s mission and programmes must align with one of the designated funding areas to be eligible for this cycle. Applicants should carefully review the specific funding opportunity before applying because the cycle uses donor-designated funds and has specific requirements. Can Faith-Based Organisations Apply? Faith-based organisations may apply when the proposed funding supports a distinct community outreach programme . Examples include programmes such as: Food banks Homelessness support Senior support services However, CCF does not fund activities undertaken for religious purposes, including worship services, religious education, faith-based materials or activities that promote a specific religion. What Information Is Required? Applicants will need to provide organisational and programme information as part of the application. The application process requires information concerning: Staffing Organisational mission Leadership Board engagement Budget Recent financial documents Existing programmes related to the selected funding area How the requested funding would strengthen existing programmes Expected impact on Charlotte County Importantly, these grants are intended to support or enhance work already underway , rather than provide funding for an organisation to begin working in an entirely new focus area. Can an Organisation Apply for More Than One Grant? No. Each organisation may submit only one application during the Fall 2026 grant cycle . Organisations should therefore carefully determine which funding opportunity most closely matches their mission and programme activities before submitting an application. How Applications Are Evaluated Applications will be reviewed by a Grants Committee consisting of trained community volunteers with relevant area expertise. The committee will assess applications based on factors including: Organisational finances Leadership Effectiveness of programmes Community impact The committee will make recommendations to the CCF Board of Directors for consideration and final approval. How Long Does the Application Take? CCF states that the application is designed to take less than two hours to complete. The programme application for the Housing Insecurity or Health Care funding areas is more detailed. Applicants are encouraged to review the available informational materials before beginning the application. Grant Information Sessions CCF strongly encourages prospective applicants to review the Fall 2026 Grant Informational Presentation recording and presentation slides before beginning an application. The information session provides an overview of: Eligibility requirements The grant cycle Application process Important dates Other relevant application information How to Apply for the Charlotte Community Foundation Grants Eligible nonprofit organisations can apply through the online grant application portal accessible through the Charlotte Community Foundation s website. Before applying, organisations should: Review the eligibility requirements. Identify the designated funding area that best matches their existing work. Review the grant information session and application guidance. Prepare the required organisational, financial and programme information. Complete the online application. Submit the application before the deadline. Apply through the Charlotte Community Foundation Grants page Application Deadline The Fall 2026 grant cycle opened on: September 1, 2026 The application deadline is: September 29, 2026 at 4:59 p.m. CCF states that deadlines are strictly enforced to ensure a fair review process. When Will Applicants Receive a Decision? Applicants will receive communication by email regarding the status of their applications in December 2026 . CCF plans for funding to be delivered before the end of December 2026 . Successful applicants will receive an award letter explaining the grant terms, including reporting acknowledgements and disbursement information. Applicants who are not selected will also receive notification by email and may contact CCF to discuss their application and learn why it was not selected. Reporting Requirements Successful grantees will be required to complete an online grant acknowledgement form within two weeks of receiving the award . One year after receiving the funding, award recipients are invited to submit a concise report of no more than three pages explaining: How the grant was used. The impact of the funding. Progress against projected outcomes. Relevant qualitative and quantitative data. About the Charlotte Community Foundation The Charlotte Community Foundation is dedicated to improving the quality of life throughout Charlotte County, Florida . The Foundation connects individuals, companies, organisations and advisors with charitable causes and permanent capital to create community impact. It has operated as a community foundation since 2004 and has granted $15 million to nearly every local nonprofit and $1.6 million in scholarships over its 20 years of service. CCF manages philanthropic resources and supports local nonprofits and students through grants and scholarships. Conclusion The Charlotte Community Foundation Fall 2026 Grants provide an opportunity for eligible nonprofits serving Charlotte County to receive financial support for existing programmes addressing important community needs. The Fall 2026 cycle focuses on five designated areas: health care, housing insecurity, seniors, veterans and youth . The Foundation is particularly offering programme grants of $15,000 for eligible organisations addressing housing insecurity and health care. Organisations interested in applying should carefully review the eligibility requirements, attend or watch the informational presentation and prepare their application before the deadline. title: Clean Slate Initiative Policy Coordinator Job 2026 | Apply for Remote Policy Position in the USA
summary: The Clean Slate Initiative (CSI) is seeking a Policy Coordinator to support its policy team through project management, policy research, technical assistance and knowledge management. The full-time position offers an annual salary of $56,000–$62,000 and is a remote role open to candidates based in the United States . Applicants must be authorised to work in the U.S. without requiring current or future visa sponsorship. The application deadline is September 15, 2026 . About The Clean Slate Initiative Founded in 2019, The Clean Slate Initiative (CSI) works across the United States and in Congress to advance laws that automatically seal eligible criminal records for people who have completed their sentences and remained crime-free. The organisation also works to expand eligibility for record sealing and promote policies that provide people with records a fair opportunity to work, pursue education, contribute to their communities and achieve their full potential. According to the supplied opportunity information, 14 states and Washington, D.C. have passed Clean Slate laws impacting more than 18 million people . CSI works with bipartisan leaders and organisations and focuses on policy design, implementation and campaign strategies that centre lived experience. About the Policy Coordinator Position The Policy Coordinator will support CSI s Policy Department through project management, policy research and technical assistance. Reporting to the Public Policy Director , the successful candidate will help maintain knowledge of record-relief policies across all 50 states, support cross-functional initiatives and develop resources that inform CSI s policy, campaign and implementation work. The role is particularly suited to someone who is highly organised, detail-oriented and interested in translating complex policy information into practical resources that help teams make informed decisions. Key Responsibilities The Policy Coordinator will contribute to the Policy Department s operations and strategic projects. Project Management and Coordination Responsibilities include: Supporting the Policy Department s day-to-day operations. Coordinating meetings and tracking tasks. Contributing to both small-scale initiatives and larger strategic policy projects. Ensuring project timelines and deliverables remain on track. Policy Tracking and Knowledge Management The successful candidate will create, maintain and update internal policy tracking tools, legislative comparison frameworks and knowledge templates related to record-relief laws across all 50 states. The role also involves tracking legislative developments using PolicyNote and maintaining accessible summaries of state policy landscapes, implementation questions and emerging trends. Policy Research The Policy Coordinator will conduct research on record-relief and related policies, including: Record sealing Expungement Automated relief Petition-based relief The candidate will also compile and organise information concerning eligibility rules, exclusions, waiting periods, procedural requirements, implementation structures and other important policy choices. Technical Assistance and Partner Support The role will involve responding to policy questions from CSI staff and supporting technical assistance, coalition and partner meetings when required. Who Should Apply? CSI is looking for a candidate with experience in policy, legislative, legal or public policy research . The ideal candidate should be: Highly organised and intellectually curious. Interested in researching and understanding detailed policy issues. Strong in project management and organisation. Exceptionally attentive to detail. Able to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines. Comfortable working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. A strong written and verbal communicator. Passionate about equitable criminal justice policy and CSI s mission. Familiar with tools such as Asana, Google Workspace, PolicyNote and Airtable , or equivalent platforms. What Success Looks Like CSI identifies several indicators of success for the Policy Coordinator. The successful candidate will be expected to: Maintain accurate and up-to-date policy tracking systems and legislative resources. Produce high-quality policy research that informs campaign strategy, implementation and technical assistance. Keep Policy Department projects organised and progressing through effective project management and follow-through. Provide timely and accurate responses to policy questions. Build strong cross-functional relationships. Contribute to a collaborative and high-performing Policy team. Professional Development Opportunity Clean Slate laws continue to evolve across different states, creating an opportunity for the Policy Coordinator to develop expertise in a rapidly changing policy environment. The role provides an opportunity to build systems, strengthen knowledge management and become a trusted internal resource on record-relief policy. Salary and Benefits The Clean Slate Initiative offers a salary range of: $56,000–$62,000 per year The final salary within this range will be determined according to qualifications and relevant experience. CSI states that its compensation package is not negotiated after an offer is made. The benefits package includes: 100% employer-paid health insurance. 100% employer-paid dental insurance. 100% employer-paid vision insurance. 6% employer 401(k) match. Pre-tax transportation benefits. Paid holidays. Paid vacation. Paid sick leave. Paid casual time off. Work Arrangement The Policy Coordinator position is full-time and remote . CSI is location-agnostic regarding where candidates are based within the United States. Candidates who live near the organisation s Orlando office may discuss a hybrid or in-office arrangement. The successful candidate must: Currently reside in the United States. Be authorised to work in the United States. Work collaboratively with colleagues across different time zones. Live close to a major airport and be able to travel approximately 10–15%. Attend required on-site planning meetings at least twice a year in various locations. Attend one all-staff learning trip and the organisation s annual convening each year. Employment Authorisation Applicants for employment in the United States must have work authorisation that does not now or in the future require visa sponsorship for U.S. employment authorisation. Therefore, international applicants who require employer sponsorship should note that this position does not provide that sponsorship. Application Timeline CSI has provided a tentative recruitment timeline for the position. Stage Date Application period August 25 – September 15, 2026 First interviews Weeks of September 21 and October 5, 2026 In-basket exercise After first interviews Panel interviews Week of October 19, 2026 Reference checks Week of October 26, 2026 Finalist interview with CEO Week of October 26, 2026 Offer extension Week of November 2, 2026 Tentative start date November 16, 2026 CSI states that applications will be reviewed continuously and encourages interested candidates to apply early. Applications received after September 15 may be considered, but consideration is not guaranteed. How to Apply Interested applicants should first familiarise themselves with the work of The Clean Slate Initiative before applying. Applicants can then submit their application through the organisation s Talent Portal. Official organisation website: The Clean Slate Initiative Apply for the Policy Coordinator position: Policy Coordinator – Official Application For questions about the job posting or application process, candidates can contact careers@cleanslateinitiative.org . Why Apply for the Policy Coordinator Role? This position offers an opportunity for a policy professional to contribute to work focused on criminal justice reform and record relief across the United States. The successful candidate will work with policy information from all 50 states, conduct research, support strategic projects and develop resources that can inform campaigns, implementation and technical assistance. The role may be particularly relevant to professionals with backgrounds in public policy, law, legislative research, criminal justice policy, policy analysis or related areas . Conclusion The Clean Slate Initiative Policy Coordinator position is a full-time remote opportunity for a policy professional interested in criminal justice reform, record relief and public policy research. The successful candidate will support research and project management while maintaining policy resources covering record-relief laws across the United States. The position offers a $56,000–$62,000 annual salary , comprehensive benefits and a remote work arrangement for candidates residing and authorised to work in the United States. Applications are being accepted through September 15, 2026 , with applications reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates who meet the requirements are encouraged to apply early because applications submitted after the deadline may not receive consideration. Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage . title: The Next Move Grant 2026: Up to €250,000 in Multi-Year Funding for Sport-Based Nonprofits in Brazil, Colombia and Argentina
summary: Organizations using sport and physical activity to tackle gender-based violence, discrimination, exclusion and harmful gender norms can apply for The Next Move , a multi-year general support funding opportunity under the United by Sport program. The initiative is designed to strengthen organizations that use sport as a vehicle for social impact and help create safer, more inclusive and cohesive communities. Selected organizations can receive €150,000, €200,000 or €250,000 over three years , with the funding divided equally across the 36-month partnership. The total funding pool is €2 million . The opportunity is particularly relevant for nonprofit and grassroots organizations working directly with communities through sport, including organizations addressing gender equality, gender-based violence prevention, inclusion, leadership opportunities for girls and young women, and positive gender norms. The Next Move Grant 2026 The Next Move is part of the United by Sport program and focuses on supporting organizations that use sport intentionally to address barriers to social cohesion. The program recognizes that sport can sometimes reproduce existing inequalities, but it can also serve as a powerful platform for positive social change. Through sport and physical activity, organizations can help people build trust, develop positive relationships, challenge discriminatory attitudes and behaviors, and strengthen their sense of belonging. The funding opportunity specifically focuses on communities in: Brazil Colombia Argentina Organizations must apply based on one country of implementation , meaning applicants cannot submit a single multi-country application covering several countries. What Is the Purpose of The Next Move? The Next Move aims to strengthen organizations that are working to create communities where people feel: Safe Valued Connected Included Able to participate meaningfully Treated fairly and equitably The program identifies several issues that can prevent people from fully participating in sport and community life. These include gender-based violence, discrimination, exclusion, unequal opportunities and harmful gender norms. Through general support funding, the adidas Foundation intends to provide organizations with the flexibility to strengthen their overall work rather than requiring them to implement one narrowly defined project. This means selected organizations can identify their own organizational priorities and determine how the funding can best support their charitable mission, programs and organizational development within the funding guidelines. Key Focus Areas The Next Move is particularly interested in organizations working on issues connected to gender, inclusion and social cohesion through sport. 1. Gender-Based Discrimination and Sexism Organizations may work to address: Gender stereotypes Sexism Unequal opportunities Discriminatory attitudes Exclusion from participation Barriers affecting girls and women in sport The objective is to help create environments where people can participate in sport and community life without facing discrimination based on gender. 2. Gender-Based Violence The program also focuses on preventing and addressing gender-based violence, including: Sexual harassment Abuse Intimate partner violence Unsafe environments Other forms of gender-based violence Sport can be used as a platform to promote safety, awareness, respectful relationships and non-violent behaviors. 3. Inclusion and Equal Participation Organizations can also contribute by creating opportunities for groups that experience exclusion or unequal access to sport. This may include initiatives that increase participation, representation and opportunities for girls, young women and non-binary young people. 4. Positive Gender Norms and Masculinities The Next Move seeks to support organizations promoting healthy, respectful and non-violent gender norms. This can include work that challenges harmful expectations surrounding gender and encourages healthier relationships and behaviors. 5. Community Connection and Social Cohesion Sport can bring people together and create opportunities for communities to build trust and stronger relationships. Organizations may therefore use sport to promote: Belonging Trust Positive relationships Community participation Cooperation Social cohesion How Much Funding Is Available? The Next Move offers three possible grant amounts: €150,000 €200,000 €250,000 The selected amount is provided over three years , meaning the grant is divided equally over the 36-month partnership. The total funding pool for the opportunity is €2 million . Organizations are not automatically guaranteed the amount they request. Following the assessment process, the adidas Foundation may offer a lower amount than the organization initially requested. Any adjustment will be discussed with the organization before the grant agreement is finalized. The partnership is expected to begin in Q1 2027 , with the grant start and first disbursement expected around March 2027 . What Is General Support Funding? Unlike a grant that requires an organization to deliver one predefined project, The Next Move provides General Support funding . This approach is designed to support the organization as a whole and give partners greater flexibility to determine their priorities. Selected organizations can use the funding to support their charitable activities and organizational priorities, provided that the proposed expenditure remains within the eligible funding categories and complies with the Foundation s requirements. Organizations will identify a small number of priorities and planned activities and report on what the funding supported, what changed and how the money was used at category level. This structure allows organizations to make adjustments during implementation when necessary, provided those adjustments remain within the approved scope and eligible uses of the grant. What Can the Grant Be Used For? The funding can support activities that directly advance an organization s charitable work or help the organization deliver its work safely, effectively, inclusively and accountably. Examples include: Sport and Community Programs Funding can support: Community-based sport and physical activity programs Inclusive sporting events Participant activities Community engagement Outreach initiatives Advocacy and awareness campaigns Coalition-building and networking Peer-learning activities Participant transportation Venue costs Activity costs Sports equipment Adaptive equipment Materials required for implementation Organizations can also use eligible funding for staff time and related expenditure directly connected to charitable program activities. Training and Capacity Building Organizations may support training for: Coaches Facilitators Community stakeholders Staff members Other individuals involved in program delivery The objective is to strengthen the organization s ability to deliver its programs effectively and safely. Safeguarding and Participant Protection Funding may also contribute to: Safeguarding policies and procedures Safeguarding training Incident reporting systems Referral procedures Participant protection measures Community protection measures Inclusion and accessibility measures Data protection Information security Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Organizations can also use eligible funding to strengthen their ability to understand and demonstrate their impact. This includes: Monitoring and evaluation Accountability systems Learning processes Participant feedback Community feedback Outcome measurement Evaluation activities MEAL systems Specialist advice related to charitable programs Organizational and Administrative Costs The grant includes an indirect cost recovery component equivalent to 20% of eligible direct costs . This component is intended to recognize that strong programs require strong organizational systems behind them. Eligible indirect costs can include areas such as: General management and administration Finance and accounting Payroll and staff resources General office expenses Operating costs Audit expenses Insurance Legal and compliance costs Organization-wide IT systems Administrative systems General fundraising and income-generation activities Organizations do not need to provide a separate expenditure breakdown for the indirect cost recovery component, although they must maintain appropriate financial records. What Cannot Be Funded? Although The Next Move provides flexible General Support funding, the grant is not completely unrestricted . The following are not eligible: Sub-granting or onward granting Non-charitable activities Activities outside the scope of the program Commercial or primarily profit-seeking activities unrelated to charitable work Support for political parties or candidates Partisan campaigning Lobbying outside the organization s charitable mission and legally permissible activities Religious proselytization or missionary work Repayment of historic deficits Unrelated loans Penalties or liabilities unrelated to eligible charitable activities Private benefits Disproportionate remuneration Illegal activities Harmful or discriminatory activities Sanctioned activities Costs that cannot be properly documented Organizations should therefore ensure that their intended use of funding is directly connected to their charitable mission and the objectives of The Next Move. Who Can Apply? The Next Move is not an individual scholarship or fellowship opportunity . It is specifically designed for non-profit organizations . Eligible organizations must be legally registered and operating in one of the three eligible countries: Brazil Colombia Argentina Organizations must use sport or physical activity as a core vehicle for creating social impact . This means sport should be central to the organization s mission, programs and approach to creating positive change in the communities it serves. Potentially eligible organizations include: Community-based sport organizations Sport-for-good organizations Sport clubs with a demonstrated social impact mission Sport foundations Women s sport networks Advocacy organizations that combine advocacy with sport-based programs Grassroots organizations delivering sport-based community services Sport clubs can qualify where their charitable mission extends beyond simply providing sporting activities to their own members. APPLY HERE Organizational Eligibility Requirements In addition to being a nonprofit organization operating in an eligible country, applicants must satisfy several organizational requirements. The organization must: Be a legally registered non-governmental organization or equivalent established for charitable or public-benefit purposes under applicable national law. Have been registered and operational for at least two years in the country where it will implement its activities at the time of full application submission. Be legally permitted to receive foreign charitable funding under applicable local law. Not engage in partisan political activity or religious proselytization. Have a statutory purpose and core mission aligned with the objectives of The Next Move and the United by Sport program. Demonstrate commitment to non-discriminatory practices across race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion and ethnicity. Have an annual grant request that does not exceed 50% of the organization s total income in its most recent completed financial year . Have appropriate governance oversight and checks and balances, such as a board or equivalent oversight body. Have basic financial controls and reliable financial records. Be able to identify, track, document and report how the adidas Foundation s funds are used. Have documented safeguarding policies and procedures. Have a safeguarding reporting mechanism explaining how concerns are raised and addressed. Have appropriate safer recruitment measures. Have documented rules covering expected and prohibited behavior, such as a Code of Conduct or Ethics Policy. Have guidance or established practices for protecting participant data and images. Not be subject to international sanctions or restrictions that would prevent a partnership. Be willing to undergo the Foundation s due diligence process. Be willing to support communications and storytelling activities in accordance with the adidas Foundation s ethical communication guidelines. Be committed to Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning processes. Income Requirements Based on the Grant Requested The organization must also have an annual income proportionate to the amount of funding it is requesting. Based on the most recent financial statement, covering 2025 or 2024 , the requirements are: Organizations requesting €150,000 Minimum annual income: €100,000 Maximum annual income: €1.5 million Organizations requesting €200,000 Minimum annual income: €135,000 Maximum annual income: €2 million Organizations requesting €250,000 Minimum annual income: €165,000 Maximum annual income: €2.5 million These financial requirements are intended to ensure that the level of funding is proportionate to the organization s existing financial capacity. Geographic Eligibility The Next Move is specifically open to organizations operating in: Brazil, Colombia and Argentina. Organizations must be legally registered and implementing their activities in the country where they are applying. Importantly, applicants cannot submit one application covering multiple countries. Each application should focus on one country of implementation . Organizations based outside Brazil, Colombia or Argentina should not assume they are eligible simply because they work internationally. The guidelines specifically identify these three countries as the geographic scope of the call. Race and Diversity Eligibility The opportunity does not specify a particular race or ethnic group that applicants must belong to because the applicants are organizations rather than individuals . However, eligible organizations must demonstrate a commitment to non-discriminatory practices across: Race Gender Gender identity Sexual orientation Age Disability Religion Ethnicity The program itself is designed around inclusion, equality, safety and social cohesion. The Application Process The Next Move uses a two-stage application process designed to allow organizations to determine whether the opportunity is suitable before investing significant time in a full application. Stage 1: Expression of Interest Organizations begin by submitting an Expression of Interest (EOI) through an online application form. The EOI includes: Eligibility screening Questions about the organization Questions about the organization s work Required document uploads The eligibility screening includes yes/no questions covering the non-negotiable organizational requirements. Stage 2: Full Application Only organizations that are shortlisted following the EOI stage will move to the full application stage. Shortlisted organizations may be asked to: Complete a self-assessment Develop a proposed plan for the first year Provide an indicative first-year budget Answer additional questions Participate in an interview with the adidas Foundation The Foundation may also arrange a short call to clarify outstanding information. This approach means applicants do not have to prepare a lengthy full proposal at the initial stage. How Applications Are Assessed After organizations submit their Expressions of Interest, the adidas Foundation reviews applications against the eligibility criteria. The process includes: EOI submission Eligibility screening Conflict-of-interest checks Shortlisting Full application Interview and additional submissions Review and final selection Due diligence Contracting Grant disbursement The Foundation intends to select a minimum of eight organizations to receive grants, subject to successful completion of the subsequent due diligence process. Due Diligence Requirements Being selected following the assessment process does not immediately guarantee funding. Organizations selected for funding must successfully complete the adidas Foundation s organizational due diligence process before funding is formally confirmed. The due diligence process examines areas including: Legal Status and Governance Organizations may need to provide: Registration or incorporation documents Current proof of legal existence Tax-status documentation Governing documents Organizational charts Governance arrangements Information about authorized representatives Financial Management The Foundation may assess: Financial position Financial sustainability Sources of income Financial statements Audit reports Accounting systems Financial controls Approval procedures Grant-tracking systems Financial records Safeguarding Organizations may need to demonstrate: Safeguarding policies Reporting mechanisms Incident-management procedures Safer recruitment practices Safeguarding responsibilities Training arrangements Integrity and Organizational Standards The review can also include: Codes of conduct Ethics policies Whistleblowing systems Complaints mechanisms Anti-fraud measures Anti-bribery measures Data protection procedures Public-domain reviews Sanctions screening Adverse-media screening Other integrity checks Organizations that do not meet the Foundation s due diligence requirements will not be eligible for funding. Community of Practice and Peer Learning Selected organizations will participate in a Community of Practice designed to encourage peer learning, exchange and collective reflection. The Community of Practice can help participating organizations: Share experiences Exchange promising practices Strengthen organizational capacity Learn from other organizations Reflect on implementation challenges Develop approaches related to gender equity Share lessons around gender-based violence prevention Explore safe sport practices Strengthen inclusion Improve community-building through sport Organizations are encouraged to designate at least one relevant staff member to participate. This could include staff working in: Programs Safeguarding MEAL Organizational development Leadership Other relevant areas Organizations are encouraged to plan for up to 60 hours per year , or approximately five hours per month, for Community of Practice activities, peer exchanges, learning events and related preparation. Participation costs, including relevant staff time, can be covered through the grant and should be reflected in the organization s proposed use of funds. Communications and Storytelling Selected organizations should also be prepared to participate in communications and storytelling activities connected to the partnership. This may involve: Contributing to storytelling pieces Providing relevant content Following approval processes Following the adidas Foundation s ethical communication guidelines Respecting brand guidelines Providing feedback and approvals within five business days The Foundation will provide selected organizations with the relevant communication and brand guidance. Reporting and Evaluation The reporting requirements are designed to be proportionate and focused on learning rather than requiring organizations to report every individual expenditure line. During the three-year partnership, selected organizations can expect several reporting and learning requirements. At the Start Organizations will complete an Organizational Self-Assessment to identify areas for growth. During the Partnership There will be: Bi-annual check-in calls with the Foundation Annual narrative reporting Annual financial reporting at category level Annual reach data Photos and videos from activities, where appropriate and with consent Annual partner feedback Financial reporting will show planned and actual expenditure, significant variances and a transaction tracker. Individual receipts and invoices do not have to be submitted as part of routine annual reporting, but organizations must retain the relevant documentation because the Foundation may request supporting records. At the End Organizations will complete: An organizational self-assessment Change stories at organizational and individual level They may also be invited to participate in a learning exercise during or after the funding period. Grant Disbursement The three-year grant period begins after the grant agreement is signed. The grant is expected to begin in Q1 2027 , with the first disbursement expected around March 2027 . Funding will be distributed in three instalments over the three-year partnership. The first instalment will be released after: Successful completion of due diligence Approval of the initial plan Approval of the budget Signing of the grant agreement Subsequent instalments will normally depend on the Foundation reviewing and accepting reporting from the previous period and approving the updated plan and budget. Key Dates and Deadline Applicants should pay close attention to the following dates: Call launch: 7 September 2026 Q A Webinar: 21 September 2026 at 11:00 AM BRT EOI submission deadline: 4 October 2026 at 11:59 PM BRT Screening and shortlisting: October 2026 EOI outcome notification: October 2026 Full application, interviews and submissions: November 2026 Review and final selection: December 2026 Vetting and due diligence: December 2026/January 2027 Contracting: January/February 2027 Expected grant start and first disbursement: March 2027 The deadline to submit the Expression of Interest is 4 October 2026 at 11:59 PM BRT . Dates after the EOI deadline are indicative and may be adjusted by the adidas Foundation. Visit HERE to learn more about The Next Move Grant 2026 How to Apply Eligible organizations should begin with the Expression of Interest (EOI) stage. The application process requires organizations to provide information about their legal status, organizational structure, work, eligibility and activities, together with the required supporting documents. The guidelines state that English is the working language throughout the application process , including the application, supporting documents, interview and partnership. At the EOI stage, unofficial translations of documents are sufficient. Organizations should ensure that the information submitted accurately reflects their own experience, activities and organizational context. Applicants are encouraged to provide specific and concrete examples from their work. Important Considerations Before Applying Organizations considering The Next Move should assess themselves against the eligibility requirements before submitting an EOI. In particular, applicants should confirm that they: Are a legally registered nonprofit organization. Have operated for at least two years in the implementation country. Are legally permitted to receive foreign charitable funding. Operate in Brazil, Colombia or Argentina. Use sport or physical activity as a central part of their social-impact approach. Work directly with communities. Do not intend to sub-grant the funding. Have appropriate governance structures. Have adequate financial controls. Meet the applicable annual-income requirement. Have safeguarding systems in place. Have appropriate data protection practices. Can participate in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning. Are prepared to undergo organizational due diligence. Can commit to a three-year partnership. Organizations should also ensure that their requested grant amount is proportionate to their annual income and that their planned activities clearly align with the objectives of The Next Move. Who Qualifies for This Opportunity? Qualifying category: Nonprofit organizations, NGOs, sport organizations, sport clubs, foundations, women s sport networks and advocacy organizations that use sport or physical activity as a core vehicle for social impact. Required organizational qualifications Applicants must generally: Be legally registered as a nonprofit/non-governmental or equivalent charitable/public-benefit organization. Have operated for at least two years in the country of implementation. Be legally allowed to receive foreign charitable funding. Directly implement activities in the country of operation. Use sport or physical activity as a central part of their mission and programs. Align their mission with The Next Move and United by Sport objectives. Meet the applicable annual-income requirements. Have appropriate governance and financial systems. Have safeguarding and reporting mechanisms. Demonstrate commitment to nondiscrimination. Be willing to undergo due diligence and integrity screening. Commit to the three-year partnership and MEAL requirements. Eligible countries/regions The opportunity is open specifically to organizations implementing activities in: Brazil, Colombia and Argentina. Applications must focus on one country of implementation rather than combining multiple countries in one application. Race and ethnicity There is no specific racial or ethnic group requirement for applicants . The applicant is an organization rather than an individual. However, eligible organizations must demonstrate nondiscriminatory practices across race, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion and ethnicity. Conclusion The Next Move Grant 2026 provides a significant opportunity for established nonprofit organizations in Brazil, Colombia and Argentina that are using sport to tackle social challenges and build stronger communities. With grants of €150,000, €200,000 or €250,000 distributed over three years , the program can support much more than individual sporting activities. Eligible funding can contribute to community programs, equipment, participant activities, training, safeguarding, monitoring and evaluation, organizational capacity and appropriate administrative costs. The opportunity is particularly relevant to organizations addressing gender-based violence, discrimination, exclusion, unequal participation and harmful gender norms through sport . Organizations interested in applying should carefully review their eligibility, financial capacity, governance, safeguarding systems and alignment with the program before submitting an Expression of Interest.
