title: Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027: $70,000 Fellowship for Interdisciplinary Researchers in Computation
summary: The Neukom Institute at Dartmouth College has announced the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Competition 2027 , an exceptional opportunity for recent PhD graduates and emerging scholars whose research crosses traditional academic boundaries and incorporates computation as a significant intellectual, methodological, or practical component. The prestigious fellowship is designed for highly motivated interdisciplinary researchers who are interested in exploring complex questions that cannot easily be confined to a single academic discipline. Successful candidates will receive the opportunity to conduct independent research at Dartmouth College while working across departments, collaborating with faculty mentors, teaching seminars, and becoming part of a vibrant intellectual community focused on computational thinking and interdisciplinary scholarship. The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship positions are scheduled to begin on September 1, 2027 . Selected Fellows will receive appointments lasting two years , with the possibility of requesting a third year . For the 2027–2028 academic year, Neukom Fellows will receive a stipend of $70,000 , alongside additional financial support for equipment, travel, and research materials. The competition provides an important platform for scholars whose work sits at the intersection of disciplines and computation. Whether computation serves as a methodological tool, a conceptual framework, or an explicit component of a research project, the fellowship encourages innovative approaches that challenge conventional academic boundaries. About the Dartmouth Neukom Institute Postdoctoral Fellows Program The Neukom Institute at Dartmouth College supports research and intellectual exploration at the intersection of computation and multiple academic disciplines. Its Postdoctoral Fellows Program brings together scholars whose work demonstrates the potential to bridge fields, develop new approaches to research, and expand how computational ideas can contribute to the understanding of complex problems. The fellowship is particularly suited to researchers who do not fit neatly into traditional academic categories. Applicants may come from disciplines across the sciences, humanities, social sciences, arts, engineering, and other fields, provided they can demonstrate a meaningful connection between their research interests and the broader theme of computation. A central feature of the Neukom Fellowship is its interdisciplinary structure. Fellows are expected to engage with faculty members and academic departments across Dartmouth College rather than working exclusively within a single disciplinary environment. The program seeks individuals who can demonstrate both: A history of successful collaboration across disciplinary boundaries; and Strong evidence of independence, initiative, and the ability to develop original research ideas. This balance between collaboration and independent scholarship makes the fellowship particularly attractive to researchers seeking to establish themselves as leaders in emerging interdisciplinary fields. Why the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Is Unique Many postdoctoral opportunities are structured around a specific department, laboratory, or narrowly defined research area. The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship takes a broader approach by encouraging scholars to connect different academic perspectives through computational research and thinking. Successful Fellows will have the opportunity to: Conduct independent interdisciplinary research. Work with faculty members from two Dartmouth College departments. Develop relationships across multiple academic disciplines. Explore innovative research questions. Engage with computational concepts and methodologies. Teach one seminar course each year. Access financial support for research activities. Participate in Dartmouth s academic and intellectual community. Build professional networks with scholars across different disciplines. Develop new approaches that move beyond conventional academic paradigms. The program recognizes that some of the most important contemporary research challenges require perspectives from multiple disciplines. By supporting scholars who can work across these boundaries, the Neukom Institute aims to encourage new forms of intellectual collaboration and discovery. Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Funding and Financial Benefits One of the major advantages of the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is the financial support provided to selected candidates. For the 2027–2028 academic year , Neukom Fellows will receive a stipend of: $70,000 In addition to the annual stipend, Fellows can access additional funding for important research-related needs. Additional support may be available for: Research equipment. Academic travel. Conference participation. Research materials. Other resources necessary to support the Fellow s scholarly work. This financial structure allows Fellows to focus significantly on their research and professional development while receiving institutional support for activities that contribute to their academic projects. The fellowship appointment is initially structured as a two-year position , providing researchers with substantial time to develop and advance an interdisciplinary research agenda. Fellows may also have the option to request a third year, depending on program arrangements and individual circumstances. Fellowship Structure and Academic Experience The Neukom Fellows Program provides more than financial support. It offers a comprehensive academic environment designed to help emerging scholars expand their research networks and intellectual perspectives. 1. Two-Year Fellowship Appointment Selected candidates will receive appointments lasting two years. This extended period gives Fellows the opportunity to undertake substantial research projects rather than focusing only on short-term academic activities. The possibility of requesting a third year may provide additional flexibility for scholars whose research requires further development. 2. Mentorship Across Two Departments One of the defining features of the program is interdisciplinary mentorship. Neukom Fellows will be mentored by faculty members representing two different departments at Dartmouth College . This structure encourages Fellows to actively engage with different intellectual traditions and methodologies. Working across departments can help researchers: Develop broader perspectives. Establish collaborations outside their original discipline. Access different methodological approaches. Test research ideas with diverse academic audiences. Build interdisciplinary professional networks. Develop innovative approaches to complex research questions. 3. Departmental Residence While Fellows will work across two academic departments, they will take up residence in one department at Dartmouth College. This arrangement provides Fellows with an academic home while simultaneously allowing them to maintain meaningful engagement with another disciplinary environment. 4. Teaching Opportunity Neukom Fellows will teach one seminar course each year on a subject related to their interests and expertise. This teaching component provides an opportunity for Fellows to: Develop university-level teaching experience. Design an original seminar. Share their research interests with students. Explore interdisciplinary topics in a classroom setting. Strengthen their academic portfolio. Gain valuable experience for future faculty and research positions. 5. Focus on Research Apart from the teaching seminar, Fellows do not have additional duties specified by the program. This allows successful candidates to devote substantial attention to their research projects, collaborations, and scholarly development. Research Focus: Computation and Interdisciplinary Scholarship A central requirement of the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is a meaningful connection between an applicant s research and the theme of computation. Importantly, computation does not necessarily have to be interpreted narrowly. According to the program description, computation may serve as: A framing concept for intellectual exploration. An explicit methodological component of research. A tool for investigating complex questions. A foundation for interdisciplinary collaboration. A means of connecting different academic fields. This broad approach makes the fellowship relevant to researchers working in a wide range of disciplines. For example, applicants may explore intersections between computation and areas such as: Computer science. Artificial intelligence. Data science. Digital humanities. Computational social science. Mathematics. Engineering. Biology. Environmental studies. Economics. Philosophy. Linguistics. Media studies. Creative arts. Public policy. History. Literature. Psychology. Physics. Education. Communication studies. Cultural studies. The specific research area does not need to belong exclusively to a computational discipline. However, applicants must clearly demonstrate how computation meaningfully intersects with their proposed work. Eligibility Requirements for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 The Neukom Institute welcomes applications from scholars across different academic backgrounds. To be eligible for the fellowship, applicants should meet the following requirements. Academic Qualification Applicants must hold or expect to receive one of the following qualifications by September 2027: PhD in any discipline. Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA). Master of Fine Arts (MFA), where applicable to the fellowship requirements. The program specifically indicates that candidates may be expected to complete their doctoral qualification by September 2027 . This makes the fellowship particularly relevant for: Recent PhD graduates. Final-stage doctoral candidates. Emerging scholars preparing to transition into postdoctoral research. Researchers seeking an interdisciplinary academic environment after completing their doctoral studies. Research Connection to Computation Applicants must demonstrate research interests that strongly intersect with the broader theme of computation. Candidates should clearly explain: How computation relates to their research. How computational ideas, methods, or frameworks contribute to their work. Why interdisciplinary collaboration is important for their proposed research. How the fellowship environment would strengthen their intellectual development. Interest in Multidisciplinary Research The Neukom Institute is specifically looking for scholars who are interested in working beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries. Applicants should therefore demonstrate: Experience collaborating across disciplines. Interest in multidisciplinary research. Openness to different academic perspectives. Ability to communicate with researchers from different fields. Willingness to explore new methodologies and intellectual frameworks. Independent Thinking and Initiative Although collaboration is important, successful applicants must also demonstrate independence. The program seeks candidates with evidence of: Original thinking. Research initiative. Intellectual independence. Leadership potential. The ability to develop and pursue innovative research questions. Ability to Think Beyond Traditional Paradigms The fellowship strongly emphasizes innovative and unconventional thinking. Applicants should demonstrate the capacity to: Challenge traditional academic boundaries. Connect ideas from different disciplines. Develop creative research methodologies. Explore emerging questions. Think critically about established assumptions. Build new intellectual frameworks. Required Application Materials Applicants for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program must prepare several important documents. Candidates are encouraged to begin preparing their applications early, particularly because identifying and contacting potential Dartmouth faculty mentors may require significant research and communication. The required application materials include the following. 1. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a comprehensive academic curriculum vitae. The CV should clearly highlight relevant experience, including: Academic qualifications. Research experience. Publications. Academic appointments. Teaching experience. Research collaborations. Conferences and presentations. Awards and honors. Technical or methodological skills. Interdisciplinary projects. Candidates should ensure that their CV clearly demonstrates their academic development and capacity to contribute to an interdisciplinary research environment. 2. Publications List Applicants are required to provide a list of publications. This may include: Journal articles. Book chapters. Books. Conference papers. Working papers. Research reports. Other relevant scholarly publications. Where appropriate, candidates should clearly identify publications that demonstrate interdisciplinary or computational aspects of their work. 3. Statement of Research Interests Applicants must submit a statement of research interests with a maximum length of two pages . The statement should include a short description of the research the applicant would like to pursue as a Neukom Fellow. A strong research statement should clearly address: The central research question. The importance of the proposed research. The relationship between the project and computation. The interdisciplinary nature of the work. The proposed methodology. Expected research outcomes. Potential academic or societal contributions. Why Dartmouth College provides an appropriate environment for the research. Because the fellowship is highly interdisciplinary, applicants should ensure that their research statement is understandable to readers from multiple academic backgrounds. 4. Proposed Departments and Faculty Mentors Applicants must describe: Which Dartmouth College departments they are interested in working with. Which Dartmouth faculty members they would like to collaborate with. Why these academic connections are relevant to their proposed research. How working across multiple departments would enhance their scholarship. The Neukom Institute strongly encourages applicants to research Dartmouth s departments and faculty listings when preparing this section. Candidates are also strongly encouraged to identify potential faculty mentors and contact them while developing their applications. This is an important part of the application strategy because demonstrating a clear understanding of Dartmouth s academic environment can strengthen the connection between the applicant s proposed research and the fellowship. Applicants should therefore consider: Identifying departments relevant to their research. Reviewing faculty profiles. Reading about faculty research interests. Identifying potential interdisciplinary connections. Contacting prospective mentors where appropriate. Explaining clearly how those academic relationships could support the proposed research. 5. Three Referees and Letters of Recommendation Applicants must provide details for three referees . The letters of recommendation should speak directly to the aims and objectives of the fellowship. Applicants will provide the referees email addresses through the application system. Referees will then receive an email with access to upload their letters directly. Applicants will not have access to the submitted recommendation letters. Candidates should carefully select referees who can discuss areas such as: Research ability. Academic independence. Interdisciplinary experience. Collaborative skills. Intellectual creativity. Leadership potential. Ability to develop innovative research. Suitability for a postdoctoral academic environment. Although applicants are encouraged to have their applications completed by the main deadline, referees have an additional period to submit their letters. 6. Optional Writing Sample or Creative Work Applicants may optionally submit one paper written in English. The work may be: Published; or Unpublished. Applicants whose work involves creative practice may submit comparable creative work instead. A strong optional submission could provide additional evidence of: Research quality. Writing ability. Originality. Methodological expertise. Interdisciplinary thinking. 7. Optional Teaching Statement Applicants may also submit a teaching statement. This can be particularly useful for candidates who want to demonstrate their readiness to teach the required annual seminar. A teaching statement may discuss: Teaching philosophy. Previous teaching experience. Approaches to interdisciplinary education. Student engagement strategies. Proposed seminar ideas. 8. Optional Cover Letter Candidates may submit an optional cover letter. A well-written cover letter could briefly summarize: Academic background. Research interests. Interdisciplinary experience. Connection to computation. Motivation for applying. Why the Neukom Fellowship is an appropriate next step. Importance of Contacting Potential Dartmouth Mentors One of the strongest recommendations provided by the program is that applicants should actively identify and contact prospective mentors at Dartmouth College. Candidates are encouraged to begin making these academic connections while drafting their applications. This approach can be valuable because it allows applicants to: Better understand Dartmouth s research environment. Identify faculty whose expertise aligns with their work. Develop stronger interdisciplinary research proposals. Explain why specific departments are relevant. Demonstrate genuine interest in collaboration. Clarify how their proposed research could fit within Dartmouth s academic community. Applicants should approach potential mentors professionally and thoughtfully. Before contacting a faculty member, candidates should: Carefully review the faculty member s research profile. Understand their major research interests. Identify a genuine connection with their own work. Prepare a concise introduction. Briefly explain the proposed research idea. Explain why the faculty member s expertise is relevant. Avoid sending generic messages to multiple academics. Early preparation is particularly important because identifying appropriate mentors and developing meaningful academic connections may take time. Residence Requirement Neukom Fellows are generally expected to be in residence at Dartmouth College. The primary exception relates to travel associated with: Research activities. Academic conferences. Other approved scholarly engagements. Candidates should therefore be prepared to participate actively in Dartmouth s academic community during the fellowship period. Being in residence provides Fellows with opportunities to: Meet regularly with faculty mentors. Participate in academic discussions. Collaborate with researchers. Engage with students. Attend seminars and events. Build interdisciplinary networks. Important Dates and Application Timeline Applicants should pay close attention to the official competition schedule. Application Site Opens August 1, 2026 The online application system becomes available through Interfolio. Application Deadline December 1, 2026 Applicants should submit their complete applications by this date. The program indicates that application review will begin on December 1, 2026. Letters of Recommendation Deadline December 8, 2026 Letters of recommendation must be submitted no later than this date. Applicants should contact their referees well in advance to ensure they have sufficient time to prepare strong recommendation letters. Fellowship Start Date September 1, 2027 Successful Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to begin their appointments. How to Apply for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 The application process is completed online through the Interfolio application platform. Interested candidates should follow these general steps. Step 1: Review the Fellowship Requirements Carefully read all eligibility criteria and application requirements before beginning the application. Ensure that your academic qualifications and research interests align with the program. Step 2: Develop Your Research Proposal Prepare a strong research statement explaining: Your proposed research. Its interdisciplinary nature. Its connection to computation. Why the research is important. How Dartmouth College would support the project. Step 3: Identify Relevant Dartmouth Departments Explore Dartmouth College s academic departments and identify those connected to your research interests. Consider how different departments could contribute complementary perspectives to your project. Step 4: Identify Potential Faculty Mentors Review Dartmouth faculty profiles and identify scholars whose research aligns with your proposed work. The program strongly encourages applicants to explore potential academic connections while preparing their applications. Step 5: Contact Potential Mentors Where appropriate, reach out professionally to prospective mentors. Explain your research interests and your interest in the interdisciplinary environment provided by the Neukom Fellowship. Step 6: Prepare Your Supporting Documents Compile the required materials, including: Curriculum vitae. Publications list. Two-page research statement. Description of relevant departments and faculty mentors. Referee information. Consider including optional materials where they strengthen your application. Step 7: Notify Your Referees Early Contact your three referees well before the deadline. Provide them with: Information about the fellowship. Your research proposal. Your CV. Relevant application deadlines. This will help them prepare letters that are specifically tailored to the aims of the Neukom Fellowship. Step 8: Submit Your Application Online Applications can be submitted through Interfolio once the application system opens. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day, as early submission provides time to address any technical issues. Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for ambitious scholars working at the intersection of disciplines. Applicants should therefore ensure that their applications clearly communicate both academic depth and interdisciplinary vision. Clearly Explain the Computational Connection Do not assume that reviewers will automatically understand how your research relates to computation. Clearly explain whether computation functions as: A research methodology. A theoretical framework. A conceptual lens. A practical tool. A core component of your proposed project. Demonstrate Genuine Interdisciplinarity Simply mentioning multiple disciplines may not be sufficient. Applicants should demonstrate how different fields will actively contribute to the proposed research. Explain: What each discipline contributes. Why one discipline alone is insufficient. How interdisciplinary collaboration will create new insights. Balance Collaboration and Independence The fellowship seeks candidates who can collaborate effectively while also pursuing independent scholarship. Use examples from your academic experience to demonstrate both qualities. Research Dartmouth Thoroughly A strong application should demonstrate why Dartmouth College is particularly suitable for the proposed project. Avoid generic statements. Instead, identify: Relevant departments. Potential faculty collaborators. Academic resources. Interdisciplinary opportunities. Select Referees Strategically Choose referees who understand your research trajectory and can provide detailed examples of your abilities. Ideally, recommendation letters should reinforce the themes emphasized throughout the application. Begin Preparation Early Because the application involves: Developing a research proposal. Identifying multiple departments. Researching Dartmouth faculty. Contacting potential mentors. Coordinating recommendation letters. Applicants should begin preparing well before the December deadline. Diversity and Equal Opportunity Dartmouth College states that it is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer with a strong commitment to diversity. The institution encourages applications from a broad spectrum of individuals, including: Women. Persons of color. Persons with disabilities. Veterans. Other legally protected groups. This commitment reflects the Neukom Institute s interest in building a diverse intellectual community that brings together different perspectives, experiences, academic backgrounds, and approaches to research. Who Should Consider Applying? The Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship may be particularly suitable for scholars who answer yes to several of the following questions: Are you completing a PhD or recently completed doctoral research? Does your work intersect meaningfully with computation? Does your research cross traditional academic boundaries? Are you interested in working with scholars from multiple disciplines? Do you have an innovative research idea that requires diverse academic perspectives? Are you comfortable developing independent research projects? Do you want postdoctoral teaching experience? Are you interested in becoming part of an interdisciplinary academic community? Can you identify Dartmouth faculty members whose expertise could strengthen your research? If these characteristics align with your academic goals, the Neukom Fellowship could provide an important opportunity to develop an innovative research agenda. Key Benefits of the Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellowship Successful Fellows can benefit from a combination of financial support, research opportunities, mentorship, teaching experience, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Key benefits include: A $70,000 stipend for 2027–2028 . A two-year fellowship appointment . The possibility of requesting a third year . Additional support for equipment. Funding support for research travel. Support for research materials. Mentorship from faculty in two Dartmouth departments . An opportunity to conduct interdisciplinary research. Residence within Dartmouth College s academic community. The opportunity to teach one seminar course per year . No additional duties beyond the specified fellowship responsibilities. Opportunities to collaborate across traditional academic boundaries. Access to an intellectually diverse research environment. Professional development through research and teaching. Opportunities to expand academic networks. Application Deadline The application deadline for the Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Competition 2027 is: December 1, 2026 Applicants should note that letters of recommendation are due no later than: December 8, 2026 The application portal opens on August 1, 2026 , and selected Fellows are expected to begin their appointments on September 1, 2027 . APPLY HERE How to Access the Official Application Interested applicants should submit their applications online through the Interfolio application platform after the application portal opens. Visit HERE to learn more about the Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027. Conclusion The Dartmouth Neukom Postdoctoral Fellows Program 2027 represents an outstanding opportunity for emerging scholars whose work challenges traditional disciplinary boundaries and engages meaningfully with the broad field of computation. With a $70,000 stipend, additional research support, mentorship across two academic departments, teaching opportunities, and a two-year appointment with the potential for extension, the fellowship provides an exceptional environment for developing ambitious interdisciplinary research. The program is particularly attractive because it welcomes researchers from diverse academic disciplines rather than restricting participation to a single field. Candidates who can demonstrate a strong connection between their research and computation, an interest in multidisciplinary collaboration, and the ability to think independently and creatively are encouraged to consider applying. Prospective applicants should begin preparing early by refining their research ideas, identifying relevant Dartmouth departments, connecting with potential faculty mentors, and securing strong recommendation letters. Given the fellowship s emphasis on innovative scholarship and interdisciplinary collaboration, a carefully developed application that clearly communicates both intellectual originality and the value of cross-disciplinary research could significantly strengthen a candidate s prospects. With applications closing on December 1, 2026 , eligible researchers have an opportunity to position themselves for a transformative postdoctoral experience at one of the leading institutions supporting interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computation and the wider academic world. title: ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 in Germany for PhD Students from Developing Countries
summary: The Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre – Aachen, Bangkok, Chennai, Dresden (ABCD-Centre) has opened applications for the ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 , an opportunity designed to support doctoral researchers from developing countries whose work addresses pressing challenges related to water security, climate change adaptation, ecosystem resilience, sustainable development, and environmental management. The 2027 scholarship call will support two doctoral students through a nine-month research stay in Germany . Successful applicants will have the opportunity to conduct research at one of three participating host institutions: RWTH Aachen University in Aachen, Technische Universität Dresden, or UNU Resource Nexus in Dresden . The research stays are scheduled to take place from March 1, 2027, to November 30, 2027 . The programme is particularly valuable for PhD researchers who want to strengthen their academic and research experience in an international environment while developing research that can ultimately be translated into practical solutions, policy recommendations, and real-world approaches to water and climate adaptation challenges. About the Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre The Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre – Aachen, Bangkok, Chennai, Dresden (ABCD-Centre) is an international collaborative initiative bringing together leading academic and research institutions in Europe and Asia. The consortium includes: RWTH Aachen University Asian Institute of Technology Indian Institute of Technology Madras United Nations University – Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and Resources (UNU Resource Nexus) Technische Universität Dresden The Centre seeks to address some of the world s most urgent and interconnected environmental challenges, particularly those involving water security and climate adaptation . Its work combines research, education, international collaboration, and knowledge transfer, with a strong emphasis on ensuring that scientific findings can move beyond academic publications and contribute to practical solutions. A major objective of the ABCD-Centre is to develop the next generation of Future Environmental Leaders . These researchers are expected not only to produce high-quality scientific work but also to help translate research findings into applications that can benefit communities, institutions, policymakers, and other stakeholders. About the ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 For the 2027 cycle, the ABCD-Centre is offering two scholarships , each supporting a nine-month research stay in Germany . The scholarships are intended for doctoral students from developing countries who are already undertaking PhD studies at universities in developing countries. The programme provides selected researchers with an opportunity to temporarily conduct part of their doctoral research at an internationally recognised German research institution. Applicants are required to indicate their preferred host university when applying. The available host institutions are: RWTH Aachen University – Aachen, Germany Technische Universität Dresden – Dresden, Germany UNU Resource Nexus – United Nations University Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and Resources, Dresden, Germany The research stay is planned for: March 1, 2027 – November 30, 2027 Applicants who are able and willing to spend the full nine-month period in Germany are given preference during the selection process. Research Areas and Thematic Clusters Applicants are encouraged to develop research proposals that fit within the three interconnected research clusters of the ABCD-Centre. Cluster I: Water Security and Water Resources Management The first cluster focuses on challenges surrounding water security and the sustainable management and provision of water resources. Research areas include: Water security Water resources management Secure water supply Water treatment Innovative approaches to water management Technologies and approaches for improving access to and sustainability of water resources This cluster may be particularly relevant to researchers investigating how societies can improve water availability, water quality, infrastructure, and resource management in the context of growing environmental pressures. Cluster II: Ecosystem Resilience and Nature-Based Adaptation The second cluster focuses on strengthening ecosystems and exploring nature-based approaches to climate adaptation. Potential areas include: Ecosystem resilience Nature-based solutions Climate adaptation Environmental restoration Sustainable ecosystem management Innovative monitoring systems Adaptation measures that work with natural processes Researchers working on environmental systems and solutions that use or strengthen natural ecosystems to address climate risks are encouraged to consider this research cluster. Cluster III: Transfer Strategies for Climate Adaptation The third cluster focuses on how climate adaptation research can be transferred into society and translated into practical action. It includes areas such as: Traditional knowledge Local economies Societal acceptance Climate adaptation strategies Knowledge transfer Policy development Community-based approaches Translating scientific findings into practical solutions This cluster recognises that effective climate adaptation requires more than scientific innovation. Solutions must also be socially acceptable, economically realistic, culturally appropriate, and capable of being implemented by communities and institutions. Priority Research Topics for the 2027 Scholarship Although the scholarship is open to a broad range of research topics connected to the ABCD-Centre s thematic clusters, priority will be given to proposals addressing five specific areas. Topic A: Modelling Water Infrastructure, Digitalization and Habitat Modelling This area includes research into: Water infrastructure modelling Innovative digitalisation methods Digital twins Habitat modelling Applicants working on the use of digital technologies, modelling systems, simulations, or related tools to improve water infrastructure or environmental management may find this theme particularly relevant. Topic B: Innovative Monitoring for Ecosystem Resilience and Nature-Based Adaptation This topic focuses on improved methods for monitoring ecosystems and understanding their resilience to environmental change. Research could address: Innovative environmental monitoring Ecosystem resilience Nature-based adaptation measures Monitoring tools and technologies Assessment of environmental adaptation strategies Topic C: Climate-Driven Water Extremes in Urban Areas This theme addresses the increasing risks that climate change creates for urban water systems. Potential research may focus on climate-driven: Flooding Water scarcity Extreme rainfall Urban water challenges Other water-related climate extremes Researchers investigating how cities can prepare for, manage, and adapt to increasingly severe water-related climate events are encouraged to consider this topic. Topic D: Sustainable Business Models for Unconventional Water Resources This research area focuses on developing sustainable approaches for the use and management of unconventional water resources. Applicants may explore: Sustainable water business models Alternative water resources Economic approaches to water management Resource efficiency Innovative approaches to water supply The theme highlights the importance of developing solutions that are not only environmentally sustainable but also economically viable. Topic E: Eco-Friendly Materials and Sustainable Building Solutions for Climate Adaptation This topic focuses on sustainable materials and construction approaches that can contribute to climate adaptation. Research may involve: Eco-friendly materials Sustainable building solutions Climate-resilient construction Environmentally sustainable infrastructure Materials that support climate adaptation Who Can Apply? The scholarship is specifically designed for doctoral students from developing countries . Applicants must satisfy the programme s stated eligibility requirements. Applicants must: Be doctoral/PhD students . Have commenced their PhD studies within the last three years . Be registered as full-time PhD students . Be enrolled at a university in a developing country . Have a research topic that can be aligned with the thematic areas of the ABCD-Centre. Be able to demonstrate strong academic and research potential. Be prepared to undertake the proposed research stay at the selected German host institution. Have the necessary support and agreement from their home institution and doctoral supervisor. The call does not specify eligibility according to race or ethnicity. Rather, its geographic eligibility is framed around doctoral students from developing countries/Global South countries who are studying at universities in developing countries. Applicants should therefore carefully establish that their home country and institution meet the programme s definition or requirements for developing-country eligibility before submitting an application. What Does the Scholarship Cover? The ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarship provides financial support intended to cover key expenses associated with the research stay in Germany. The scholarship typically includes support for mobility, accommodation and living expenses, insurance, and travel . The stated financial components include: Monthly accommodation and living expenses Selected scholars will receive: €1,200 per month This allowance is intended to contribute towards accommodation and living costs during the research stay. Insurance allowance The scholarship provides an insurance allowance of up to: €105 per month The exact amount is subject to the programme s stated maximum. Travel allowance A one-time travel expense stipend of up to: €1,000 is available to support travel expenses associated with the research stay. Research materials and equipment In addition to the personal allowances, up to €1,000 may be allocated for research project materials and equipment through the host institution. This additional funding can provide valuable support for researchers who require specific materials, equipment, or other research-related resources to conduct the approved project. Duration of the Research Stay Each scholarship lasts for nine months . The research stay is scheduled to run from: March 1, 2027, to November 30, 2027. Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate their willingness to spend the complete nine-month period in Germany. Preference is given to candidates who are willing to undertake the full research stay rather than only a shorter period. Available Host Institutions Applicants must identify their preferred host institution as part of the application. RWTH Aachen University The first option is RWTH Aachen University , located in Aachen, Germany. Applicants interested in undertaking their proposed research at RWTH Aachen should identify a suitable host scientist and, preferably, obtain an invitation letter from the prospective host. Technische Universität Dresden The second option is Technische Universität Dresden (TU Dresden) . Researchers whose projects align with the university s relevant expertise may select TU Dresden as their preferred host institution. UNU Resource Nexus The third option is the UNU Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and Resources (UNU Resource Nexus) , located in Dresden. This option may be particularly relevant for applicants working on integrated approaches to resources, environmental management, water, sustainability, and related areas. Application Documents Applicants are required to compile their application materials into one single PDF file . The application should contain the following documents: 1. Personal motivation for the research stay Applicants must provide a 2–3 page motivation statement explaining their motivation for undertaking the research stay. The statement should clearly communicate why the applicant wants to participate, how the research stay fits into their doctoral project, and how the proposed experience will contribute to their academic and professional development. 2. Sample of a scientific paper Applicants must provide a sample of a written scientific paper . This gives the selection committee an opportunity to assess the applicant s academic writing and research capabilities. 3. Recent Curriculum Vitae A current CV should be included, highlighting relevant: Academic qualifications Research experience Publications Professional experience Awards Projects Skills Other achievements relevant to the proposed research 4. Preferred host university Applicants must clearly indicate which of the three participating institutions they prefer: RWTH Aachen University Technische Universität Dresden UNU Resource Nexus 5. Support letter from the home institution A support letter from the applicant s home institution is required. This is important because the research stay forms part of the applicant s ongoing doctoral work and requires institutional support. 6. Invitation letter from a host scientist An invitation letter from a prospective host scientist is preferably included. While the wording indicates that this is preferred rather than listed as an absolute mandatory document, applicants should make every reasonable effort to establish contact with an appropriate host researcher before applying. 7. Statement regarding online work Applicants must provide a statement demonstrating their ability to work online if remote work is required . This requirement is relevant to the practical organisation of the research stay and any circumstances in which some research activities may need to be undertaken remotely. 8. Enrollment certificate and transcript Applicants must submit: An enrollment certificate from their home institution A current transcript of records These documents must be no older than six months . 9. Passport copy A copy of the applicant s passport must also be included in the application. Agreements Required Before Applying Before submitting the application, the applicant s doctoral supervisor and home university must agree on several important aspects of the proposed research stay. These include the following. Research topic The applicant, supervisor, and home institution should agree on a research topic that is aligned with the ABCD-Centre s research clusters and priorities. Doctoral project timeline A detailed timeline of the entire doctoral project must be established. This should show how the proposed nine-month research stay fits into the applicant s broader PhD programme. Research project in Germany Applicants must describe the specific research project they intend to conduct in Germany. This description should include: The research objectives Activities to be undertaken A timetable How the research contributes to the overall PhD Plans for future third-party funded research projects Outreach contributions Applicants should also describe their planned contributions to the ABCD-Centre s outreach activities . This highlights the programme s emphasis on knowledge sharing and communication beyond the immediate research project. How Will Applicants Be Selected? Selection is based on several factors. The ABCD-Centre s Steering Committee is responsible for carrying out the selection process. Key selection considerations include: Academic merit Applicants should demonstrate strong academic performance and research potential. Motivation The committee will consider the applicant s motivation to contribute meaningfully to the relevant environmental field. A strong application should therefore explain not only why the applicant wants to travel to Germany, but also why the proposed research matters and what impact it could have. Quality of the research proposal The quality and relevance of the proposed research project are central to the selection process. Applicants should demonstrate: A clear research problem Well-defined objectives A logical methodology Relevance to the ABCD-Centre Potential practical applications A realistic timeline Potential contribution to policy or practice Commitment to the full research stay Preference is given to candidates who are willing to spend the full nine months in Germany . Policy relevance Applicants who are interested in translating research findings into policy papers are also given preference. This reinforces the programme s objective of connecting academic research with practical environmental and policy solutions. English proficiency and communication Proficiency in English is considered important. Applicants should also demonstrate effective communication skills because the programme involves international academic collaboration, research exchange, and outreach activities. Adaptability The ability to adapt to conducting research in Germany is another important consideration. Successful applicants should be prepared to work within an international research environment and collaborate with researchers from different academic and cultural backgrounds. Reporting Requirements Successful scholarship recipients will have responsibilities beyond simply completing their research stay. Scholarship and experience report A mandatory scholarship and experience report must be submitted three months before the scholarship ends . Recipients should therefore keep records throughout the research stay that can help them prepare the required report. Scientific draft paper Before the end of the research stay, scholars must submit a scientific draft paper based on the research conducted during the fellowship. The paper should demonstrate the scientific outcomes of the research stay. The draft may subsequently be developed further into a publication. This requirement means that applicants should approach the nine-month stay with a clear plan for generating tangible research outputs. Rules and Regulations The scholarship operates under the applicable rules and regulations of: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) The German Federal Foreign Office The relevant host institutions Upon selection, scholarship recipients will be required to sign a contract with their host institution. The contract will outline the terms of the scholarship and expected conduct during the research stay. Advice for Prospective Applicants Applicants should begin preparing well before the deadline because the application requires multiple documents and institutional coordination. A strong applicant should consider the following steps: Confirm your eligibility by checking that you are a full-time PhD student at a university in a developing country and that your PhD began within the last three years. Review the ABCD-Centre research clusters and identify where your doctoral research fits. Consider the five priority topics and determine whether your project can directly address one of them. Identify your preferred German host institution based on research fit rather than simply selecting an institution because of its reputation. Identify potential host scientists whose research interests align with your proposed project. Seek a host invitation letter early , since the call preferably requests one. Discuss the proposed research stay with your PhD supervisor and home university and obtain the required institutional support. Develop a strong research plan showing what you will accomplish during the nine months. Prepare your motivation statement carefully , explaining the academic, research, practical, and policy value of the proposed stay. Update your CV and select a strong scientific paper that demonstrates your research and writing ability. Obtain recent academic documents , making sure the enrollment certificate and transcript are not more than six months old. Prepare the required statement about online work if remote work becomes necessary. Ensure all documents are combined into one PDF file before submission. Submit the application before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day. Application Deadline The application deadline for the ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 is: October 31, 2026 Applications must be submitted by email to: abcd-centre@rwth-aachen.de Applicants should compile all required documents into a single PDF file and send it to the stated email address before the deadline. Contact and Further Information For questions concerning the scholarship and application process, applicants can contact the ABCD-Centre directly at: abcd-centre@rwth-aachen.de Applicants are also encouraged to seek guidance from their local International Office and DAAD office , particularly regarding questions related to the research stay in Germany. For more scholarships opportunities visit OFY Website HERE Why This Scholarship Is a Valuable Opportunity The ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarship offers more than financial assistance. For a doctoral researcher from a developing country, a nine-month research stay at a leading German academic or research institution can provide exposure to international research networks, specialised expertise, new methodologies, research infrastructure, and potential future collaborations. The programme is also strongly focused on translating research into practical solutions . This makes it particularly suitable for researchers who want their work to influence environmental policy, planning, technology, community-level solutions, or sustainable development practices. The opportunity can also help scholars develop research outputs, international connections, and experience that may support future academic collaborations and third-party research funding. Conclusion The ABCD Future Environmental Leaders Scholarships 2027 provide an international research opportunity for doctoral students from developing countries working on important challenges related to water security, climate adaptation, ecosystem resilience, nature-based solutions, sustainable infrastructure, and environmental management. With two nine-month scholarships available, successful applicants will be able to conduct research at RWTH Aachen University, Technische Universität Dresden, or UNU Resource Nexus in Germany from March 1 to November 30, 2027 . The scholarship provides €1,200 per month for accommodation and living expenses , an insurance allowance of up to €105 per month , a one-time travel stipend of up to €1,000 , and potentially up to €1,000 for research materials and equipment through the host institution . Candidates should pay particular attention to the quality and practical relevance of their research proposal, their motivation, academic record, institutional support, and potential contribution to the ABCD-Centre s work. Eligible doctoral students should begin preparing their applications early and submit the complete application as one PDF to abcd-centre@rwth-aachen.de by October 31, 2026. title: PhD Position in Medical Imaging AI at the University of Zurich and AWS: Apply for a PhD in 3D Medical Imaging, AI and Computer Vision
summary: The Department of Quantitative Biomedicine at the University of Zurich (UZH) is inviting applications for a PhD position focused on Medical Imaging AI , offering an opportunity for researchers interested in artificial intelligence, computer vision, medical image computing and clinically relevant machine learning research. The PhD position is jointly affiliated with the University of Zurich (UZH) and the University Hospital Zurich (USZ) , with the possibility of an additional affiliation with the ETH AI Center for an appropriate candidate. The research will also be conducted in active collaboration with the AWS for Healthcare team , giving the successful candidate an opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced AI research, medical imaging and real-world healthcare applications. The position is particularly relevant to candidates with academic backgrounds in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering or closely related disciplines who have a strong interest in medical applications of artificial intelligence and are motivated to develop and scale AI algorithms through the AWS ecosystem. Host Institutions and Research Environment The position is hosted by the Department of Quantitative Biomedicine at the University of Zurich and is jointly affiliated with the University Hospital Zurich . The research environment also has strong connections to ETH Zurich , with the possibility for a suitable candidate to affiliate with the ETH AI Center. A distinctive feature of this opportunity is the collaboration with the AWS for Healthcare team . Rather than focusing solely on theoretical or laboratory-based research, the PhD will combine methodological research with direct clinical relevance and opportunities to translate research outcomes into practical algorithms and applications. This makes the position particularly attractive for researchers who want to develop expertise not only in artificial intelligence and medical imaging but also in the transition of research innovations into real-world healthcare technology. Research Areas for the PhD The PhD position focuses on several interconnected areas of medical imaging artificial intelligence. Applicants should be prepared to engage with advanced computational methods and their application to medical data. 1. Vision-Language Modeling for 3D Medical Imaging One of the central research directions is vision-language modeling (VLM) for three-dimensional medical imaging . Vision-language models seek to connect visual information with language-based information. In the context of medical imaging, this can involve developing AI systems capable of understanding complex medical images and relating their visual content to textual descriptions, clinical findings or other forms of medical knowledge. The position specifically highlights work involving 3D medical imaging , including research associated with CT imaging and the CT-RATE dataset. This research area has significant potential applications in medical image interpretation, automated reporting, clinical decision support and multimodal healthcare AI. 2. Image Segmentation Another major research focus is medical image segmentation . Image segmentation involves identifying and delineating specific structures, organs, tissues, lesions or other clinically relevant regions within medical images. For a PhD researcher, this area may involve developing machine learning and deep learning approaches that can accurately identify structures within complex medical images and improve the reliability of automated medical image analysis. The position references research including CADS and vesselFM as part of its segmentation and visual grounding focus. 3. Visual Grounding The PhD will also address visual grounding , an area concerned with linking language or semantic descriptions to specific regions or objects within visual data. In medical imaging, visual grounding can contribute to AI systems that do more than simply classify an image. Such systems can potentially identify and associate particular anatomical structures or abnormalities with corresponding clinical concepts or descriptions. This creates an important connection between computer vision, natural language processing and medical image understanding. 4. Clinical Validation The research will not stop at developing AI models. A major component of the position is clinical validation , meaning that developed approaches will need to be assessed for their usefulness and performance in medically relevant settings. This clinical orientation is one of the defining features of the opportunity. The research will combine methods-driven artificial intelligence research with direct clinical relevance through the UZH and University Hospital Zurich environment. 5. Benchmarking and Public Challenges The PhD researcher will also have the opportunity to participate in public benchmarking initiatives . Benchmarking allows researchers to compare AI systems using common datasets, evaluation procedures and performance measures. It can help determine whether a proposed method provides meaningful improvements over existing approaches. The position specifically references initiatives including VLM3D and BRATS . Participation in such initiatives can also help researchers build an international research profile and contribute to the broader medical AI research community. What the PhD Position Offers The University of Zurich s opportunity provides an interdisciplinary research environment combining academic research, healthcare and industry collaboration. According to the official position announcement, successful candidates can benefit from several important opportunities. 1. Research at the Intersection of AI and Medicine The position combines advanced computational and AI methods with direct clinical applications. This means the PhD researcher will have the opportunity to investigate sophisticated artificial intelligence methods while considering how those methods can address real healthcare and medical imaging challenges. 2. Affiliation with Leading Swiss Research Institutions The position is based at UZH and USZ and has strong ties to ETH Zurich. For an appropriate candidate, there is also the possibility of affiliation with the ETH AI Center , providing an additional connection to Switzerland s highly developed artificial intelligence research ecosystem. 3. Collaboration with AWS for Healthcare The successful researcher will work closely with the AWS for Healthcare team and participate in joint activities. This provides exposure to an industry environment alongside academic and clinical research. For candidates interested in developing AI systems that can eventually operate at scale, this industry connection may be particularly valuable. 4. Translating Research into Real-World Applications The PhD offers an opportunity to contribute to the translation of research into real-world algorithms and applications within the AWS ecosystem . This practical orientation can help bridge the gap between academic research and technology implementation. 5. Access to Clinical Collaborators The position provides access to clinical collaborators, enabling researchers to work in an environment where medical expertise can inform the development and evaluation of AI systems. This is especially important in medical AI because successful models need to address real clinical requirements rather than simply perform well on technical datasets. 6. Curated Medical Datasets The researcher will have access to curated datasets relevant to medical imaging research. High-quality datasets are essential for developing, training and evaluating machine learning systems, particularly in specialized areas such as 3D medical imaging. 7. Modern Computing Infrastructure The position also provides access to modern computational infrastructure, including AWS cloud computing resources . This can be important for computationally intensive research involving large medical imaging datasets and advanced AI models. Who Is Eligible to Apply? The position is aimed at candidates with a strong technical and research background relevant to artificial intelligence and medical image computing. The official announcement identifies the following candidate profile. Academic Background Applicants should have a degree in: Computer Science Physics Mathematics Engineering Or a closely related field The position is therefore particularly suited to graduates whose academic training provides a strong foundation in quantitative, computational or technical research. Interest in the Medical Domain An intrinsic interest in the medical domain is required . The university indicates that this interest should ideally be demonstrated through previous academic work, such as a related Master s thesis or research project . Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate more than a general interest in artificial intelligence. A convincing application should explain why the applicant is interested in applying AI and computational methods to healthcare and medical imaging. Interest in AWS and Scalable AI Applicants are also expected to have a genuine interest in working with AWS to establish and scale algorithms and applications through the AWS ecosystem. Candidates should therefore consider highlighting any relevant experience or interest in areas such as: Machine learning Deep learning Computer vision Medical image analysis Cloud computing Artificial intelligence Data science Algorithm development Research software Scalable computing systems Who Can Apply? The official announcement does not specify a particular nationality, race, ethnicity or continent restriction . The listed eligibility requirements focus primarily on academic background, interest in medical research and motivation to work with AWS. Therefore, based on the published criteria, the opportunity can be considered open to qualified applicants internationally rather than being restricted to applicants from a particular country or continent. Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may be considered provided they satisfy the academic and research requirements. The announcement does not identify a nationality or racial restriction. However, applicants should rely on the official university announcement for any additional admission, immigration, employment or doctoral-registration requirements that may apply during the application or enrollment process. Application Requirements Interested candidates are required to submit three key documents. 1. Curriculum Vitae Applicants should submit an updated CV highlighting their academic background, research experience, technical skills, projects, publications and other experience relevant to medical AI and computational research. Where applicable, candidates should emphasize experience with: Artificial intelligence Machine learning Deep learning Computer vision Medical imaging Image segmentation Natural language processing Vision-language models Data science Programming Cloud computing Research projects Scientific publications 2. Transcript of Records Applicants must provide their transcript of records . The transcript helps demonstrate the candidate s academic preparation and performance. Candidates should ensure that the submitted transcript is clear and readable and adequately reflects their relevant academic coursework. 3. Brief Statement of Motivation Applicants must also submit a brief statement of motivation . This document should explain why the candidate is interested in the PhD position and why their academic and research background makes them suitable for the project. A strong motivation statement should connect three major elements: Your academic and technical background Your interest in medical imaging and AI Your motivation to work with UZH, USZ and AWS Rather than simply stating that you are interested in artificial intelligence, the statement should demonstrate how your previous studies, research projects or technical experience have prepared you for the proposed research area. How to Apply Applications should be sent directly by email to: bjoern.menze@uzh.ch Applicants should include: CV Transcript of records Brief statement of motivation The email subject line should clearly state: “PhD Position UZH-AWS” APPLY HERE Application Deadline The official UZH webpage currently states the deadline as 31 September 2026 . However, September has only 30 days , meaning 31 September is not a valid calendar date. In addition, a recent post by the research group supervisor, Prof. Bjoern Menze, has publicly indicated 30 September 2026 as the deadline. Applicants should therefore treat 30 September 2026 as the likely intended deadline and, importantly, confirm the deadline directly with UZH before submitting. Because the official university webpage itself contains the apparent date error, applicants should avoid waiting until the final day and should submit their applications as early as possible. How to Make Your Application Competitive This is a specialized PhD opportunity, so applicants should carefully demonstrate their suitability rather than submitting a generic doctoral application. 1. Demonstrate Technical Preparation Show evidence of your ability to work with quantitative and computational research. Relevant coursework, research projects, programming experience and technical projects can strengthen your application. 2. Connect Your Experience to Medical Imaging If you have previously worked on medical imaging, biomedical engineering, healthcare AI, computer vision or related research, make this connection explicit. If your background is primarily in computer science or another technical discipline, explain clearly how you intend to apply your existing expertise to medical research. 3. Explain Your Interest in AI for Healthcare The project is not simply an AI research position. It is specifically concerned with medical imaging AI . Your motivation statement should therefore explain why you want to work on healthcare applications and what makes this research area particularly meaningful to you. 4. Highlight Research Experience Where applicable, mention: Master s research Research assistant positions Academic publications Conference presentations Machine learning projects Computer vision projects Medical research projects Open-source contributions Relevant software or technical projects 5. Demonstrate Interest in Industry Collaboration Because the PhD involves close collaboration with AWS for Healthcare, applicants should demonstrate that they are interested in translating research into practical applications. Experience working with industry, cloud technologies, applied AI projects or scalable computational systems can therefore be useful to highlight. 6. Explain Your Long-Term Research Goals A strong application should demonstrate how the PhD fits into your broader research and professional ambitions. For example, candidates may explain their interest in developing AI systems that can improve medical image interpretation, clinical decision-making, healthcare efficiency or biomedical research. Why This PhD Opportunity Stands Out The UZH-AWS PhD position brings together four important components that are increasingly influential in modern healthcare research: Artificial Intelligence + Medical Imaging + Clinical Research + Cloud Technology The combination provides a distinctive research environment. Instead of developing AI models in isolation, researchers will have opportunities to work with clinical collaborators, medical datasets and industry partners while investigating advanced approaches such as vision-language modeling, segmentation and visual grounding. The position also provides exposure to benchmarking and clinical validation, allowing research outcomes to be evaluated against established standards and potentially translated into practical healthcare applications. Visit HERE for more information about the PhD Position in Medical Imaging AI at the University of Zurich and AWS. Key Details at a Glance Opportunity: PhD Position in Medical Imaging AI Host: University of Zurich Clinical affiliation: University Hospital Zurich Potential additional affiliation: ETH AI Center Industry collaborator: AWS for Healthcare Location: Zurich, Switzerland Research area: Medical image computing and artificial intelligence Major research topics: 3D vision-language modeling, image segmentation, visual grounding, clinical validation and benchmarking Eligible academic backgrounds: Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering and closely related disciplines Medical interest: Required AWS interest: Required Application documents: CV, transcript of records and brief motivation statement Application method: Email Application email: bjoern.menze@uzh.ch Required subject line: “PhD Position UZH-AWS” Deadline stated on official page: 31 September 2026, which is an invalid calendar date Likely intended deadline: 30 September 2026, based on the research group s public announcement Nationality restriction: None stated in the published eligibility criteria Opportunity category: PhD Position / Doctoral Research Opportunity Conclusion The PhD Position UZH-AWS in Medical Imaging AI offers an opportunity for technically trained researchers to pursue doctoral research at the intersection of artificial intelligence, medical imaging and healthcare. With research spanning 3D vision-language modeling, image segmentation, visual grounding, clinical validation and benchmarking , the project is designed for candidates who want to tackle challenging problems in medical image computing while maintaining a strong connection to real-world clinical applications. The collaboration between the University of Zurich, University Hospital Zurich and AWS for Healthcare , together with potential links to the ETH AI Center, creates a multidisciplinary environment in which doctoral research can connect academic innovation with practical healthcare technology. Applicants with backgrounds in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, Engineering or related disciplines should carefully assess their academic preparation, research interests and motivation for working in medical AI before applying.
