title: Giving Joy Grant 2026: Apply for Up to $500 to Launch or Expand a Women-Focused Business or Community Project Worldwide
summary: Women entrepreneurs, aspiring business owners, nonprofit founders, and community changemakers around the world can now apply for the Giving Joy Grant 2026. The initiative provides microgrants of up to $500 USD to support innovative ideas that create meaningful economic and social benefits for women, girls, families, and communities. Giving Joy receives thousands of applications during each grant cycle, making the program highly competitive. However, the organization emphasizes that applicants do not need polished proposals or sophisticated business plans to stand out. Instead, successful applications are expected to demonstrate practical ideas, creativity, initiative, feasibility, and a clear potential for community impact. Beginning in 2026, Giving Joy has introduced a simplified global grant model with two grant cycles per year. Unlike previous regional rounds, each cycle is now open to eligible women entrepreneurs and changemakers from anywhere in the world. The Fall 2026 Giving Joy Microgrant Round opened on September 1, 2026, offering women globally an opportunity to secure funding to start or expand businesses, nonprofit organizations, NGOs, charities, projects, and other initiatives focused on improving the lives of women, girls, families, and communities. About the Giving Joy Grant Giving Joy is an organization committed to supporting women entrepreneurs and empowering women to transform innovative ideas into initiatives that generate meaningful social and economic impact. The Giving Joy Grant provides financial support to women who have practical and creative ideas but may lack the resources needed to take the next step. The funding can support a wide range of initiatives, provided they are legal and demonstrate benefits beyond individual financial gain. Applicants are encouraged to think broadly about how their ideas can contribute to positive change. A proposal may involve launching a new business, expanding an existing enterprise, establishing a nonprofit organization, implementing a community project, delivering skills training, or developing an innovative initiative that benefits women and families. The program is particularly interested in projects that create multiplied impact. This means that successful proposals should demonstrate how a relatively small amount of funding can create benefits that extend beyond the applicant herself. For example, a woman may use the grant to organize skills training for unemployed women, establish a community-based initiative that creates income opportunities, conduct educational workshops, or develop a project that improves access to knowledge, leadership opportunities, safety, or economic independence. Giving Joy Grant 2026 Funding Amount Successful applicants may receive grants of up to $500 USD. The exact amount awarded may be determined by Giving Joy based on several factors, including: The proposed activities. The applicant s project budget. The feasibility of the proposal. The potential social and economic impact. The availability of funding. How effectively the proposed grant amount will support the initiative. Applicants should therefore provide a clear and realistic explanation of how they intend to use the requested funding. A strong application should not simply state that the applicant needs money for a business or project. Instead, applicants should clearly demonstrate exactly how the funding will be spent and what outcomes are expected. For instance, applicants may need to explain: What materials they intend to purchase. What activities they plan to organize. Who will participate. How many people are expected to benefit. What the estimated costs will be. How the grant will contribute to long-term impact. 2026 Giving Joy Grant Cycle Beginning in 2026, Giving Joy has moved to a new grant structure consisting of two global grant cycles each year. The organization previously conducted multiple regional grant rounds. However, after reviewing feedback from applicants and volunteer reviewers, Giving Joy determined that operating four cycles created unnecessary administrative complexity. The new approach is designed to create a simpler, more transparent, and more effective application process. According to the organization, the new structure will help: Provide clearer timelines for applicants. Improve the quality and depth of application reviews. Reduce administrative burdens. Allow the organization to provide better support to grant recipients. Improve communication and fundraising efforts. Ensure women entrepreneurs from all regions have access to the same global application opportunities. Most importantly, each cycle is open to eligible women entrepreneurs and changemakers worldwide without dividing applicants into regional categories. Giving Joy Grant 2026 Timeline Cycle 1 – Spring 2026 The first Giving Joy Grant Cycle for 2026 has already closed. The timeline was as follows: Applications opened: April 1, 2026. Application deadline: April 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Awards announced: August 2026. The Spring 2026 round attracted significant global interest, receiving 6,423 applications from women entrepreneurs around the world. Despite the extremely competitive application pool, Giving Joy awarded 10 microgrants during the cycle. This demonstrates both the global popularity of the program and the importance of submitting a clear, specific, and impactful application. Cycle 2 – Fall 2026 Giving Joy Microgrant Round The second and current Giving Joy Grant Cycle for 2026 opened in September. The Fall 2026 Microgrant Round follows the schedule below: Applications open: September 1, 2026. Application deadline: September 30, 2026. Review period: October 1 to November 30, 2026. Shortlisted applicants notified: During the review period. Unsuccessful application notification: Applicants who have not heard from Giving Joy by December 1 should consider their applications unsuccessful. Awards announced: Beginning of December 2026. Giving Joy Grant 2026 Deadline The deadline to apply for the Fall 2026 Giving Joy Microgrant Round is: September 30, 2026. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Given the high number of applications received during each grant cycle, it is important to carefully complete all sections of the online application form and ensure that the proposed project is clearly explained. Who Can Apply for the Giving Joy Grant? The Giving Joy Grant is designed to support women aged 18 years and above. One of the major strengths of the program is its global accessibility. Applicants are not restricted to specific countries, regions, continents, or territories. Eligible women can apply from anywhere in the world. Applicants may include women who want to: Start a new business. Expand an existing business. Launch a nonprofit organization. Develop an NGO initiative. Establish a charity project. Implement a community-based initiative. Organize a training program. Create employment opportunities. Develop an innovative social enterprise. Implement a specific activity benefiting women or families. Applicants do not necessarily need to own an existing business before applying. This means that women with innovative ideas who are still at the planning stage can also submit applications. What Types of Projects Can Be Funded? Giving Joy does not limit applications to a specific industry, professional sector, trade, occupation, or craft. Applicants can propose projects from a wide range of fields. However, the proposed business, organization, project, or initiative should demonstrate clear benefits for women, girls, families, or communities. Potential areas may include: Women s entrepreneurship. Skills development. Vocational training. Community development. Education. Social enterprises. Employment creation. Women s leadership. Economic empowerment. Legal awareness. Community workshops. Professional training. Creative enterprises. Agriculture. Technology initiatives. Crafts and trades. Environmental projects. Family support initiatives. All proposed activities must be legal. Giving Joy is particularly interested in projects that create opportunities beyond the applicant s individual financial interests. For example, a business that creates employment or training opportunities for other women may demonstrate stronger community impact than a proposal focused solely on personal income. What Giving Joy Looks for in Grant Applications Giving Joy evaluates applications based on several important criteria. Applicants should carefully consider these factors when developing their proposals. 1. Alignment With Giving Joy s Mission The proposed initiative should support the broader mission of empowering and inspiring women. Projects should ideally contribute to areas such as: Women s leadership. Economic independence. Dignity. Opportunity creation. Entrepreneurship. Community empowerment. Applicants should demonstrate how their idea contributes to positive outcomes for women and their communities. 2. Social and Economic Impact Giving Joy places significant emphasis on projects that can create meaningful benefits. A strong application should explain how the proposed activities will positively affect: Women. Girls. Families. Communities. Applicants should clearly identify the people who will benefit and explain the expected outcomes. For example, rather than simply stating that a project will empower women, applicants should provide specific details about what empowerment will look like in practice. This could include: Training 20 women in a professional skill. Creating income opportunities for mothers. Providing educational workshops. Supporting women to understand their legal rights. Establishing a community enterprise. Creating employment opportunities. Developing leadership programs. Specific and measurable impact is generally more compelling than broad statements. 3. Innovation and Creativity Giving Joy prioritizes creative and innovative ideas. Applicants are encouraged to propose approaches that address genuine challenges faced by women and communities. Innovation does not necessarily mean using advanced technology or creating something that has never existed before. Instead, applicants can demonstrate innovation by: Developing a creative solution to a local problem. Combining existing approaches in a new way. Creating a practical community-based model. Identifying an overlooked challenge. Designing an initiative with multiplied benefits. The key is to demonstrate initiative and thoughtful problem-solving. 4. Effective Use of the $500 Grant Applicants must explain how the grant funds will be used. Giving Joy expects applicants to provide a practical and specific budget. A strong budget should identify: The materials or resources required. Estimated costs. Planned activities. Expected outputs. Number of beneficiaries. Applicants should avoid vague statements such as the money will help grow my business. Instead, they should provide concrete information. For example: Purchase training materials for a vocational workshop. Rent a venue for community training sessions. Purchase equipment necessary to provide a service. Develop educational resources. Support the implementation of a specific community activity. The proposed use of funds should be realistic within the $500 funding limit. 5. Clarity and Feasibility The application should be easy to understand. Applicants do not need to use complicated language or highly polished writing. Giving Joy specifically emphasizes that practical ideas and real community impact are more important than sophisticated writing. However, the application should clearly explain: What the applicant intends to do. Why the project is needed. Who will benefit. How the grant will be used. What outcomes are expected. The proposal should also be realistic and achievable within the six-month grant period. How to Write a Strong Giving Joy Grant Application Given the high number of applications received during each grant cycle, applicants should take time to develop clear responses. Here are some important strategies for preparing a competitive application. Be Specific About Your Project Avoid general statements. Clearly explain what you plan to do and how you intend to implement the activities. For example, instead of saying: I want to empower women through training. Explain: I plan to organize a practical skills training program for 15 unemployed women in my community, focusing on a specific skill that can help participants generate income. Specific proposals help reviewers understand the project and evaluate its feasibility. Clearly Identify the Beneficiaries Explain exactly who will benefit from the project. Consider questions such as: Are the beneficiaries unemployed women? Young women? Mothers? Girls? Rural communities? Women entrepreneurs? Families facing economic challenges? Also explain approximately how many people will benefit. Demonstrate Community Impact Giving Joy is interested in projects that create benefits beyond personal business growth. Applicants should explain how the initiative can generate wider social or economic impact. For example, an applicant might propose: Training 10 women in construction skills. Providing legal education workshops for 20 women. Establishing a community initiative that creates income opportunities. Creating skills programs that enable participants to support their families. The stronger the explanation of multiplied impact, the stronger the proposal may be. Develop a Clear Budget Applicants should show exactly how they plan to spend the funding. A simple budget may include: Equipment or materials. Training resources. Venue costs. Transportation directly related to project activities. Implementation costs. Every expense should connect directly to the proposed project. Focus on Practical Impact Giving Joy values real-world outcomes. Applicants should therefore focus on practical questions such as: What problem does the project solve? Who experiences the problem? What activities will address it? What changes will happen after implementation? How many people will benefit? A proposal that clearly answers these questions will be easier for reviewers to evaluate. Activities Giving Joy Does Not Primarily Fund Applicants should carefully review the restrictions before submitting their applications. Giving Joy indicates that it does not primarily fund activities focused mainly on: Purchasing merchandise or inventory for resale. Advertising. Marketing activities. Personal expenses that are not connected to broader community impact. This does not mean applicants cannot propose business-related ideas. However, the proposal should demonstrate that the funding will contribute to wider economic or social benefits rather than simply supporting individual commercial activities. Applicants should therefore carefully explain the community value of their projects. Grant Duration Successful applicants will have up to six months to implement their proposed projects. The six-month grant period gives recipients time to organize activities, use the awarded funds, and deliver the proposed outcomes. Applicants should therefore develop projects that can realistically be implemented within this timeframe. When planning an application, it may be helpful to create a simple implementation schedule covering: Project preparation. Purchase of necessary materials. Participant identification. Activity implementation. Community engagement. Monitoring of outcomes. Completion of project deliverables. A realistic implementation plan can demonstrate that the applicant has carefully considered how the project will move from idea to execution. Can Applicants Apply in Languages Other Than English? Yes. Giving Joy accepts applications in any language that can be translated using Google Translate. This significantly improves accessibility for women entrepreneurs and changemakers from different linguistic backgrounds. Applicants should still ensure that their responses are clear and understandable. Simple and direct language may be particularly useful because the organization emphasizes that clear, practical ideas are more important than polished writing. How Does the Giving Joy Application Process Work? The Giving Joy application process involves several stages. Step 1: Submit the Online Application Applications must be submitted online through the official application platform. Giving Joy does not accept proposals or funding requests submitted through email. Applicants must therefore use the designated online application form. Step 2: Application Compliance Review After submission, Giving Joy reviews applications to ensure they meet the basic requirements. The organization may contact applicants if additional information or clarification is needed. Applicants may also be asked to provide supporting information, including photos of themselves or their businesses or organizations. Step 3: Application Evaluation Giving Joy staff evaluate eligible applications based on criteria such as: Alignment with the organization s mission. Innovative use of grant funding. Social and economic impact. Community benefits. Feasibility. Clarity of the proposed activities. Step 4: Shortlisting Based on the evaluation process, Giving Joy may shortlist approximately 10 applications per grant round. Due to the large number of applications received, the organization only contacts shortlisted applicants. Step 5: Final Evaluation Giving Joy Board Members evaluate shortlisted applicants using similar assessment criteria. Board members may contact applicants to request additional information or clarification. Step 6: Grant Notification Successful applicants are notified individually via email. If an applicant does not receive communication from Giving Joy within the stated notification period, the application should be considered unsuccessful. For the Fall 2026 cycle, applicants who have not heard from Giving Joy by December 1, 2026, should consider their applications unsuccessful. Step 7: Grant Agreement and Project Implementation Successful applicants will participate in discussions with Giving Joy regarding: Grant terms and conditions. Project deliverables. Implementation guidelines. Grant agreement requirements. Once the grant agreement is signed, recipients will have up to six months to implement their proposed projects. Can You Apply More Than Once? Applicants can only submit one application per grant cycle. Women who are unsuccessful may apply again during future grant cycles. However, applicants who have already received a Giving Joy grant cannot apply again. Applicants should therefore ensure that they submit their strongest possible proposal during each application cycle. What Happens if You Win the Giving Joy Grant? Successful applicants may receive funding of up to $500 USD. The award amount will depend on: The proposed activities. The project s financial requirements. The availability of funding. Giving Joy s funding decision. Successful grantees will also receive guidance regarding grant implementation requirements. Recipients will need to review and sign a grant agreement before beginning implementation. The organization will then expect grantees to implement their proposed activities within the designated six-month period. Why the Giving Joy Grant Is a Valuable Opportunity The Giving Joy Grant is particularly valuable because it provides accessible microfunding to women with ideas that may otherwise struggle to secure traditional investment or large grants. Many funding opportunities require applicants to have established organizations, extensive financial records, or complex proposals. Giving Joy offers a different approach by emphasizing initiative, creativity, practical planning, and community impact. Key advantages of the program include: Funding of up to $500 USD. Open to women worldwide. Applicants do not need to own an existing business. Supports businesses, nonprofits, NGOs, charities, and community projects. No restriction to a specific professional field. Applications accepted in multiple languages. Focus on innovative and creative ideas. Six months available for project implementation. Opportunity to create social and economic impact. Accessible online application process. Although the funding amount is relatively modest, the program recognizes that small amounts of capital can create significant change when used strategically. Important Tips Before Applying Before submitting your Giving Joy Grant application, consider the following checklist: Confirm that you are eligible to apply. Ensure you are applying only once during the current cycle. Complete every section of the application form. Clearly explain your proposed project. Identify the women, girls, families, or communities who will benefit. Explain the social and economic impact. Provide a realistic budget. Show exactly how the grant funds will be used. Demonstrate creativity and initiative. Ensure your project is legal. Avoid proposals focused primarily on inventory resale, advertising, marketing, or unrelated personal expenses. Ensure your project can be implemented within six months. Submit your application before the deadline. Keep your project description practical and easy to understand. APPLY HERE How to Apply for the Giving Joy Grant 2026 Interested applicants must submit their applications online through the official Giving Joy Microgrant application form. Email applications and funding proposals are not accepted. Applicants should carefully review the application questions and provide complete, specific, and practical answers. Visit HERE to learn more about the Giving Joy Grant 2026. Conclusion The Giving Joy Grant 2026 presents an important funding opportunity for women entrepreneurs, aspiring business owners, nonprofit founders, and community changemakers who have innovative ideas capable of creating meaningful social or economic impact. With grants of up to $500 USD, the program supports initiatives that go beyond individual financial growth and demonstrate clear benefits for women, girls, families, and communities. The opportunity is particularly accessible because applicants do not need to own an existing business, proposals can come from any legal field, and women from countries around the world are eligible to apply. However, competition is expected to be intense. Giving Joy receives thousands of applications during each grant cycle and awards only a limited number of microgrants. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a clear, specific, creative, and practical project with measurable community benefits. For the Fall 2026 cycle, eligible applicants should submit their online applications by September 30, 2026 , and ensure that their proposals clearly demonstrate how the funding will create meaningful and lasting impact. title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28: HK$344,400 Annual Stipend for International PhD Students in Hong Kong
summary: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS) 2027/28 is now accepting applications from outstanding prospective doctoral students from around the world who want to pursue full-time PhD studies at participating universities in Hong Kong. Established by Hong Kong s Research Grants Council (RGC) in 2009, the scheme was created to attract high-achieving researchers and talented doctoral students from around the world to Hong Kong s universities. The programme is open to applicants regardless of their country of origin, prior work experience or ethnic background , making it a genuinely international doctoral fellowship opportunity. For the 2027/28 academic year , the scheme will award 400 PhD fellowships . The current official scheme information lists an annual fellowship stipend of HK$344,400 , together with an annual HK$14,400 conference and research-related travel allowance , with fellowship support provided for up to three years. The application period for the 2027/28 intake runs from 1 September 2026 to 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time . Late initial applications will not be considered. What Is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme? The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme is a competitive doctoral fellowship programme established by the Research Grants Council to attract talented researchers to Hong Kong. The scheme supports students seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at participating Hong Kong universities. Rather than restricting applications to applicants from a particular country or region, the scheme is designed to attract talented doctoral candidates internationally. The programme is therefore relevant to prospective PhD students from: Africa Asia Europe North America South America Oceania Other regions around the world The official eligibility information states that applicants are considered irrespective of their country of origin, prior work experience and ethnic background. What Makes the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Special? One of the major attractions of the HKPFS is the level of financial support available to successful fellows. For the current fellowship information published by the Research Grants Council, each awardee receives: HK$344,400 per year in fellowship stipend. HK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel. Fellowship support for up to three years . Potential additional support from the chosen university if the PhD requires more than three years to complete. For the 2027/28 academic year, 400 PhD fellowships will be awarded. Hong Kong universities normally begin their academic year in September. The travel allowance is particularly valuable for doctoral researchers who need to attend academic conferences, present research findings or undertake research-related travel. Who Can Apply for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship? The scheme is open to individuals seeking admission as new full-time PhD students at one of the participating Hong Kong universities. Applicants can come from any country or region, and the scheme does not restrict eligibility based on ethnic background or previous work experience. However, applicants must satisfy the admission requirements of the university and specific PhD programme they choose. In addition to meeting university admission requirements, applicants should demonstrate strong qualities in several areas. These include: Outstanding academic performance Research ability or potential Strong communication and interpersonal skills Excellent leadership abilities These characteristics form an important part of the fellowship s selection process. Academic Excellence Is a Major Selection Factor The HKPFS selection process places particular emphasis on academic excellence. However, academic results are not the only factor considered. The selection panels also assess: Research ability and potential. Communication and interpersonal skills. Leadership abilities. This means that applicants should present themselves as well-rounded researchers rather than relying exclusively on academic grades. A strong application should demonstrate both academic achievement and evidence that the applicant has the potential to become an independent and impactful researcher. Research Ability and Potential Research capability is another major component of the selection process. Applicants should be able to demonstrate their potential to undertake doctoral-level research successfully. This may be reflected through: Previous research projects. Undergraduate or master s research. Research publications. Conference presentations. Research-related work experience. A well-developed proposed research direction. Evidence of analytical and problem-solving abilities. The selection process considers not only what applicants have already achieved but also their potential for future research. Communication and Interpersonal Skills The fellowship also considers communication and interpersonal skills. Doctoral researchers frequently work with supervisors, research teams, academic institutions and researchers from different countries. Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate that they can: Communicate research ideas clearly. Work effectively with others. Participate in academic discussions. Build professional relationships. Present ideas to different audiences. Leadership Abilities Leadership is also one of the four major criteria used in the HKPFS assessment. Applicants should consider how their academic, professional, research or community experiences demonstrate leadership potential. Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a formal leadership position. Evidence of taking initiative, leading projects, contributing to research teams or creating meaningful academic or community impact can help demonstrate leadership potential. Participating Universities Applicants can apply for PhD programmes at the following eight participating universities: 1. City University of Hong Kong City University of Hong Kong is one of the participating institutions where HKPFS applicants can pursue eligible doctoral programmes. 2. Hong Kong Baptist University Hong Kong Baptist University is another participating university offering doctoral study opportunities under the scheme. 3. Lingnan University Lingnan University is included among the eight participating institutions. 4. The Chinese University of Hong Kong The Chinese University of Hong Kong participates in the HKPFS and offers doctoral programmes across a broad range of disciplines. 5. The Education University of Hong Kong The Education University of Hong Kong is also part of the participating university network. 6. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University The Hong Kong Polytechnic University participates in the scheme and provides PhD opportunities across multiple academic and research areas. 7. The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology is another participating institution. 8. The University of Hong Kong The University of Hong Kong, one of the region s major research universities, is also included in the scheme. The Research Grants Council confirms that applicants can seek admission as new full-time PhD students at these eight universities. How Many Universities Can You Apply To? Applicants may choose a maximum of two programmes within one or two participating universities for their PhD study. This means applicants should carefully research their preferred programmes before completing the initial HKPFS application. Candidates should consider: The university s research strengths. The specific PhD programme. Potential supervisors. Research facilities. Programme requirements. University-specific application deadlines. The suitability of the programme for their proposed research. HKPFS Application Process Applying for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme involves more than completing the initial fellowship application. Applicants must complete the HKPFS initial application and also submit full PhD admission applications to their selected universities. Step 1: Identify Your Preferred PhD Programme Applicants should first identify suitable PhD programmes at the participating universities. Research the programmes carefully and ensure that you meet their specific admission requirements. Step 2: Submit the HKPFS Initial Application The initial application is submitted through the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme Electronic System (HKPFSES) . For the 2027/28 intake, the application system is open from: 1 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time until: 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time . Step 3: Obtain Your HKPFS Reference Number After submitting the initial application, applicants receive an HKPFS Reference Number . This reference number is important because applicants must use it when communicating with the RGC and when submitting applications to their selected universities. Applicants should save the confirmation email containing their reference number and login information. Step 4: Submit Full Applications to the Universities Completing the HKPFS initial application is not enough. Applicants must also submit a full PhD admission application to the university or universities selected in their initial application. The university applications must be submitted before the individual universities own deadlines. The universities may have different application deadlines, so candidates should check each institution carefully. An initial HKPFS application that is not followed by the required university application will be considered void and will not be processed further by the RGC. University Admission Requirements Still Apply Applicants should understand that receiving an HKPFS fellowship is separate from satisfying the admission requirements of the selected university and PhD programme. Candidates must comply with the relevant university s: PhD admission requirements. Application procedures. Programme requirements. Application deadlines. Other applicable university regulations and policies. Universities will normally conduct interviews as part of their assessment process. Selection Panels Shortlisted applications are assessed according to the applicant s area of study. The scheme has two major selection panels: Sciences, Medicine, Engineering and Technology This panel considers applications relating to scientific, medical, engineering and technological areas. Humanities, Social Sciences and Business Studies This panel considers research in humanities, social sciences and business-related areas. The panels consist of experts in the relevant areas. How Applicants Are Assessed The four main selection criteria are: 1. Academic Excellence The academic record of the applicant is a primary consideration. Candidates should demonstrate strong academic performance and the ability to succeed at doctoral level. 2. Research Ability and Potential Applicants should demonstrate their capacity and potential to conduct high-quality research. 3. Communication and Interpersonal Skills The panels assess whether candidates can communicate effectively and work successfully with others. 4. Leadership Abilities Applicants should demonstrate leadership potential through their academic, professional, research or other relevant experiences. The RGC states that academic excellence is the prime consideration , while the other three areas are also taken into account. What Happens If You Are Not Selected for the Fellowship? Not being selected for the HKPFS fellowship does not necessarily mean that the applicant cannot pursue a PhD in Hong Kong. Candidates who are not selected for the fellowship may still be accepted by the university for regular PhD admission . In some cases, universities may offer successful university applicants a postgraduate studentship or other financial support. Therefore, applicants should still submit their university applications even though fellowship selection is competitive. Application Fee The Research Grants Council does not charge an application fee for the HKPFS . However, individual universities may charge their own application or processing fees. Applicants should therefore check the fee requirements of each university to which they apply. Important Application Rule: Submit Only One Initial HKPFS Application Applicants should be particularly careful about the number of initial HKPFS applications they submit. Only one initial application is accepted per applicant. Submitting multiple initial applications can result in disqualification of all applications , even if a university subsequently nominates the applicant for the fellowship. Applicants who accidentally submit multiple applications are advised to contact the RGC immediately before the application deadline. Application Language The initial HKPFS application must be completed in English , except for the field requiring an applicant s name in Chinese where applicable. Applicants should therefore ensure that the information provided in the initial application is clear, accurate and consistent. Keep Your Information Consistent The RGC cross-checks information submitted through the HKPFS system with information provided in university applications. Applicants should therefore ensure that: Personal information is accurate. Academic information is consistent. Research information is consistent. University choices match the initial application. Programme information is correct. Supporting information does not conflict between applications. Inconsistencies or incomplete information may result in an application not being considered. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The application deadline for the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 is: 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time (HKT). The application period begins on 1 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time . Late initial applications will not be considered. Applicants should also remember that the universities have their own application deadlines, which may differ from the HKPFS deadline. Important Dates Event Date Application opens 1 September 2026 Application opening time 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time Application deadline 1 December 2026 Application deadline time 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time Academic year 2027/28 Number of fellowships 400 The RGC s current announcement confirms that the 2027/28 application round opened on 1 September 2026 and closes on 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time . Fellowship Duration and Additional Support The fellowship provides the stated annual stipend and research-related travel allowance for up to three years . If an awardee needs more than three years to complete the PhD, additional support may be available from the university where the student is enrolled. Applicants requiring additional support should contact their chosen university directly for information about its policies and funding arrangements. Expected Academic Experience The HKPFS is intended for students who want to undertake full-time doctoral research in Hong Kong. Successful fellows will become part of the research communities at their selected universities and pursue doctoral research under the academic supervision and requirements of their chosen programme. The participating universities cover a wide range of disciplines, allowing applicants from different academic backgrounds to explore doctoral opportunities across areas such as: Humanities Social sciences Business Engineering Technology Medicine Science Other research disciplines offered by participating institutions The precise programmes available under the fellowship depend on the participating universities and their individual PhD offerings. Who Should Consider Applying? The HKPFS may be particularly suitable for students who: Want to pursue a full-time PhD in Hong Kong. Have an excellent academic record. Have strong research potential. Want to develop an international research career. Have strong communication and interpersonal abilities. Have demonstrated leadership potential. Are prepared to meet university-specific PhD admission requirements. Can identify suitable research programmes at participating universities. The scheme is particularly competitive, so applicants should carefully develop their academic and research profiles before applying. Preparing a Competitive Application Although the RGC identifies academic excellence as the primary consideration, applicants should also pay close attention to the other three assessment areas. A strong candidate should aim to demonstrate: Strong Academic Performance Your academic record should show your ability to perform successfully at postgraduate level. Clear Research Potential Your research background and proposed doctoral direction should demonstrate your potential to conduct meaningful and high-quality research. Strong Communication Your application should communicate your academic interests and research goals clearly. Leadership Potential Your academic, professional, community or research experiences should demonstrate initiative and leadership potential where applicable. What Applicants Should Do Before the Deadline Prospective applicants should avoid waiting until the final day of the application period. A practical preparation process would be to: Research the eight participating universities. Identify suitable PhD programmes. Review programme-specific admission requirements. Identify potential supervisors where appropriate. Review university application deadlines. Prepare academic and research information. Complete the HKPFS initial application. Record and save the HKPFS Reference Number. Submit full applications to the selected universities. Check that all information is accurate and consistent. Confirm that applications are submitted before the relevant deadlines. Official Application Information Applicants should use the official Research Grants Council information when preparing their applications. The official HKPFS 2027/28 application system is available through the Research Grants Council s electronic application platform. Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme official application information Applicants should also check the individual university websites for programme-specific admission requirements and deadlines. Visit HERE to learn more about the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 Conclusion The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 is a major international doctoral fellowship opportunity for high-achieving students seeking to pursue full-time PhD studies at participating universities in Hong Kong. The scheme will provide 400 fellowships for the 2027/28 academic year, while the current official fellowship information lists an annual stipend of HK$344,400 and an additional HK$14,400 annual allowance for conference and research-related travel , for up to three years. The opportunity is open internationally, with applicants considered regardless of their country of origin, prior work experience or ethnic background . However, candidates must meet the relevant admission requirements of their chosen university and PhD programme. Applicants should remember that the fellowship application and university admission application are connected but separate steps. Completing the initial HKPFS application alone is not sufficient; applicants must also submit their full PhD applications to their selected universities before the universities individual deadlines. The application window for the 2027/28 intake opened on 1 September 2026 , and the deadline is 1 December 2026 at 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time . Late initial applications will not be considered. For students with strong academic records, research potential, communication skills and leadership abilities, the HKPFS offers an opportunity to pursue advanced doctoral research in Hong Kong while receiving substantial financial fellowship support. title: IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026: Apply for a USD 1,000 Reporting Grant in Chiang Rai, Thailand
summary: Applications are open for the IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026 , a three-month reporting initiative designed to support original, accurate, evidence-based and ethically produced journalism about migration in Chiang Rai and surrounding areas of northern Thailand. Organized by the International Organization for Migration in Thailand, the programme will select five fellows , each of whom will receive a USD 1,000 reporting grant alongside professional mentorship, editorial guidance, programme check-ins, a field visit and potential publication through IOM platforms. The fellowship will run from 1 October to 31 December 2026 , while completed stories must be submitted by 8 January 2027 . Applications must be submitted no later than 22 September 2026 . The official announcement does not specify a closing time, so candidates should avoid waiting until the final day. Review the official IOM Thailand announcement . About the Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme Migration is an important part of Thailand’s social, economic and demographic landscape. Its significance is particularly visible in Chiang Rai, a northern border province where communities, economies and personal experiences are closely connected to cross-border mobility. Despite the importance of migration, public discussion can sometimes be shaped by incomplete information, stereotypes, sensational reporting or narratives that fail to reflect the realities and contributions of migrants. Journalism plays a significant role in determining how migration is understood by communities, institutions and policymakers. The Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme seeks to strengthen the ability of local journalists and emerging media practitioners to produce reporting that is: Accurate and based on credible evidence. Balanced in its treatment of complex migration issues. Sensitive to the dignity, safety and rights of migrants. Connected to the realities of Chiang Rai and surrounding areas. Constructive in how it contributes to public understanding. Professionally and ethically produced. Capable of challenging stereotypes and misleading migration narratives. The programme’s central theme is the reframing of migration narratives and public perceptions to encourage greater inclusion of migrants. Through well-researched stories grounded in evidence, local realities and migrants’ experiences, fellows are expected to help build a more informed and constructive understanding of migration at the local level. Read the official call for proposals . The initiative is made possible through financial support from the Government of Japan . See the programme announcement from IOM Thailand . Main Objectives of the Programme The fellowship is intended to move beyond short-term awareness raising by providing selected participants with practical support to research, produce and complete substantial migration stories. Its main objectives include: Supporting local migration journalism The programme provides financial and professional assistance for reporting on migration issues connected to Chiang Rai and nearby areas. Improving the accuracy of migration reporting Fellows will be encouraged to use reliable evidence, appropriate sources and properly verified information when developing their stories. Promoting balanced and ethical storytelling The programme emphasizes journalism that avoids harmful stereotypes, respects the dignity of migrants and accurately represents complex migration experiences.
